WMDP was developed by a consortium of academics and technical consultants, and was stringently filtered to eliminate sensitive information prior to public release. WMDP serves two roles: first, as an evaluation for hazardous knowledge in LLMs, and second, as a benchmark for unlearning methods to remove such hazardous knowledge. To guide progress on unlearning, we develop RMU, a state-of-the-art unlearning method based on controlling model representations. RMU reduces model performance on WMDP while maintaining general capabilities in areas such as biology and computer science, suggesting that unlearning may be a concrete path towards reducing malicious use from LLMs. We release our benchmark and code publicly at https://wmdp.ai

papers.title: Autonomous frequency locking for zero-offset microcomb
papers.abstract: Stabilization of carrier-envelop-offset frequency ($f_{\mathrm{ceo}}$) in a microcomb typically relies on an additional optical or microwave reference. Here we propose autonomous frequency locking, in which Kerr comb formation and quadratic frequency conversion cooperate within a single microcavity to establish a zero-offset comb from one continuous-wave pump. The internal second-order interaction supplies phase-sensitive feedback that pins $f_{\mathrm{ceo}}$ to zero while the repetition rate self-adjusts to an integer division of the pump frequency. A second-order Adler-type equation links the locking threshold to the $χ^{(2)}$ coupling strength and modal photon numbers. Simulations support this prediction and demonstrate recovery of the locked phase after perturbation. To explore a minimal realization of this mechanism, we further analyze a three-mode $χ^{(3)}$ optical parametric oscillator whose signal and idler fields are coupled through $χ^{(2)}$ conversion. Together, these interactions lock the signal and idler fields to $2/3$ and $4/3$ of the pump frequency. This configuration enables fractional-harmonic synthesis and provides a zero-offset frequency grid for measuring $f_{\mathrm{ceo}}$ with only one-third-octave spectral coverage. Our results establish internal frequency conversion as a route to autonomous microcomb control.

papers.title: Neur2BiLO: Neural Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization deals with nested problems in which a leader takes the first decision to minimize their objective function while accounting for a follower's best-response reaction. Constrained bilevel problems with integer variables are particularly notorious for their hardness. While exact solvers have been proposed for mixed-integer linear bilevel optimization, they tend to scale poorly with problem size and are hard to generalize to the non-linear case. On the other hand, problem-specific algorithms (exact and heuristic) are limited in scope. Under a data-driven setting in which similar instances of a bilevel problem are solved routinely, our proposed framework, Neur2BiLO, embeds a neural network approximation of the leader's or follower's value function, trained via supervised regression, into an easy-to-solve mixed-integer program. Neur2BiLO serves as a heuristic that produces high-quality solutions extremely fast for four applications with linear and non-linear objectives and pure and mixed-integer variables.

papers.title: Quantifying the Functional Size of Large-Scale Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: Large-scale quantum networks enable distributed quantum tasks by sharing entanglement between distant nodes. Since entanglement distribution in such networks relies on stochastic local operations and classical communication (SLOCC), the resulting end-to-end entanglement degrades with path length and exhibits statistical variations, limiting the usable range while also making the quantification of its functional size challenging. Here, we develop a statistical framework to quantify a network's functional size by analyzing the statistics of end-to-end entanglement connections established through arbitrary entanglement-distribution protocols. This framework yields a global network metric in the form of the graph radius of viable regions up to which the distributed entanglement meets specified task thresholds. In addition to identifying absolute viable regions, within which a task is guaranteed to satisfy the prescribed thresholds, the framework identifies probabilistic viable regions, within which the task succeeds with a specified confidence. Further, it yields the viable node fraction, defined as the expected fraction of network nodes accessible from a given source node for the task, and reveals that network topology strongly influences the number of nodes contained within a network's viable region, even when the viable radii are identical. Applying the framework to quantum key distribution on random networks reveals sharp threshold behavior in the viable node fraction showing that small improvements in elementary-link quality can produce a rapid increase in the viable node fraction of the network. Viable regions in a quantum network obtained using our statistical framework therefore provide a task-oriented characterization of quantum-network functionality allowing comparison of entanglement-distribution strategies and network designs.

papers.title: Optimized experiment design and analysis for fully randomized benchmarking
papers.abstract: Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely used strategy to assess the quality of available quantum gates in a computational context. RB involves applying known random sequences of gates to an initial state and using the statistics of a final measurement step to determine an effective depolarizing error per step of the sequence, which is a metric of gate quality. Here we investigate the advantages of fully randomized benchmarking, where a new random sequence is drawn for each experimental trial. The advantages of full randomization include smaller confidence intervals on the inferred step error, the ability to use maximum likelihood analysis without heuristics, straightforward optimization of the sequence lengths, and the ability to model and measure behaviors that go beyond the typical assumption of time-independent error rates. We discuss models of time-dependent or non-Markovian errors that generalize the basic RB model of a single exponential decay of the success probability. For any of these models, we implement a concrete protocol to minimize the uncertainty of the estimated parameters given a fixed time constraint on the complete experiment, and we implement a maximum likelihood analysis. We consider several previously published experiments and determine the potential for improvements with optimized full randomization. We experimentally observe such improvements in Clifford randomized benchmarking experiments on a single trapped ion qubit at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). For an experiment with uniform lengths and intentionally repeated sequences the step error was $2.42^{+0.30}_{-0.22}\times 10^{-5}$, and for an optimized fully randomized experiment of the same total duration the step error was $2.57^{+0.07}_{-0.06}\times 10^{-5}$. We find a substantial decrease in the uncertainty of the step error as a result of optimized fully randomized benchmarking.

papers.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
papers.abstract: The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, fragility of quantum states under measurement, etc. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet. Considering quantum networks, we present practical bottlenecks for secure communication, delegated computing, and resource distribution among end nodes. In particular, we show that the device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) network of isotropic states with parameter $p$ has a finite diameter depending on $p$. Motivated by the power of abstraction in graph theory (in association with quantum information theory), that allows us to consider the topology of a network of users spatially separated over long distances around the globe or separated as nodes within the small space over a processor or circuit within a same framework, we consider graph-theoretic quantifiers to assess network robustness and provide critical values of communication lines for viable communication over quantum Internet. We consider some quantum networks of practical interest, ranging from satellite-based networks connecting far-off spatial locations to currently available quantum processor architectures within computers, and analyze their robustness to perform quantum information processing tasks. Some of these tasks form primitives for delegated quantum computing, e.g., entanglement distribution and quantum teleportation, that are desirable for all scale of quantum networks, be it quantum processors or quantum Internet.

papers.title: Quartet currents in a biased three-terminal diffusive Josephson junction
papers.abstract: Biasing a three-terminal Josephson junction (TTJ) with symmetrical voltages $0,V,-V$ leads to new kinds of DC currents, namely quartet Josephson currents and phase-dependent multiple Andreev reflection (MAR) currents. We study these currents in a system where a normal diffusive metallic node $N$ is connected to three terminals $S_{0,1,2}$ by barriers of arbitrary transparency. We use the quantum circuit theory to calculate the current in each terminal, including decoherence. In addition to the stationary combination $φ_Q=φ_1+φ_2-2φ_0$ of the terminal phases $φ_i$, the bias voltage $V$ appears as a new and unusual control variable for a DC Josephson current. A general feature is the sign changes of the current-phase characteristics, manifesting in minima of the quartet ``critical current". Those sign changes can be triggered by the voltage, by the junction transparency or by decoherence. We study the possible separation of quartet currents from MAR currents in different regimes of parameters, including an "funnel" regime with very asymmetric couplings to $S_{0,1,2}$. In the regime of low transparency and asymetric couplings, we provide an analytic perturbative expression for the currents which shows an excellent agreement with the full numerical results.

papers.title: Płonka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{Płonka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for Płonka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Properties of Multi-Treatment Covariate Adaptive Randomization Procedures for Balancing Observed and Unobserved Covariates
papers.abstract: Applications of CAR for balancing continuous covariates remain comparatively rare, especially in multi-treatment clinical trials, and the theoretical properties of multi-treatment CAR have remained largely elusive for decades. In this paper, we consider a general framework of CAR procedures for multi-treatment clinal trials which can balance general covariate features, such as quadratic and interaction terms which can be discrete, continuous, and mixing. We show that under widely satisfied conditions the proposed procedures have superior balancing properties; in particular, the convergence rate of imbalance vectors can attain the best rate $O_P(1)$ for discrete covariates, continuous covariates, or combinations of both discrete and continuous covariates, and at the same time, the convergence rate of the imbalance of unobserved covariates is $O_P(\sqrt n)$, where $n$ is the sample size. The general framework unifies many existing methods and related theories, introduces a much broader class of new and useful CAR procedures, and provides new insights and a complete picture of the properties of CAR procedures. The favorable balancing properties lead to the precision of the treatment effect test in the presence of a heteroscedastic linear model with dependent covariate features. As an application, the properties of the test of treatment effect with unobserved covariates are studied under the CAR procedures, and consistent tests are proposed so that the test has an asymptotic precise type I error even if the working model is wrong and covariates are unobserved in the analysis.

papers.title: Solvable subgroup theorem, length function and topological entropy
papers.abstract: We prove a general solvable subgroup theorem in terms of length functions. As applications, we obtain a solvable subgroup theorem in dynamical systems: any solvable group of finite Hirsch length acting on a smooth manifold with uniformly positive topological entropies must be virtually $\mathbb{Z}^{n}.$ Some applications to group actions on cubical complexes and injective spaces, interval exchange transformations, and RFRS groups are also discussed.

papers.title: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
papers.abstract: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines. However, so far, a concrete mechanism by which parallel timelines can be created has never been satisfactorily formulated in a way that makes the relationships between the timelines clear. In this paper, we propose such a mechanism based on the Everett (many-worlds) interpretation of quantum mechanics. The timelines in our model are variants of the "worlds" of the Everett interpretation that can connect to each other via the time machine. They are created by the entanglement of the time machine with the environment and the resulting decoherence; therefore, we call them "entangled timelines" or E-CTCs. As the entanglement gradually spreads out to additional systems, the timelines spread out as well, providing a local and well-defined mechanism for branching timelines. The E-CTC model is similar to Deutsch's familiar D-CTC model but differs from it mainly by imposing a different consistency condition, based on pure states, which allows the information about the entanglement to be preserved. These differences allow us to create a clearer practical definition of the timelines and avoid some of the surprising consequences of the D-CTC model's non-linear evolution.

papers.title: Tensor Networks Meet Neural Networks: A Survey and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Tensor networks (TNs) and neural networks (NNs) are two fundamental data modeling approaches. TNs were introduced to solve the curse of dimensionality in large-scale tensors by converting an exponential number of dimensions to polynomial complexity. As a result, they have attracted significant attention in the fields of quantum physics and machine learning. Meanwhile, NNs have displayed exceptional performance in various applications, e.g., computer vision, natural language processing, and robotics research. Interestingly, although these two types of networks originate from different observations, they are inherently linked through the typical multilinearity structure underlying both TNs and NNs, thereby motivating a significant number of developments regarding combinations of TNs and NNs. In this paper, we refer to these combinations as tensorial neural networks~(TNNs) and present an introduction to TNNs from both data processing and model architecture perspectives. From the data perspective, we explore the capabilities of TNNs in multi-source fusion, multimodal pooling, data compression, multi-task training, and quantum data processing. From the model perspective, we examine TNNs' integration with various architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Graph Neural Networks, Transformers, Large Language Models, and Quantum Neural Networks. Furthermore, this survey also explores methods for improving TNNs, examines flexible toolboxes for implementing TNNs, and documents TNN development while highlighting potential future directions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive survey that bridges the connections among NNs and TNs. We provide a curated list of TNNs at https://github.com/tnbar/awesome-tensorial-neural-networks.

papers.title: Inference for Non-Stationary Heavy Tailed Time Series
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of inference for linear autoregressive heavy tailed non-stationary time series. Using the framework of time-varying infinite order moving average processes we show that there exists a suitable local approximation to a non-stationary heavy tailed process by a stationary process with heavy tails. This enables us to introduce a local approximation-based estimator which estimates consistently time-varying parameters of the model at hand. In addition, we study a robust self-weighting approach that enables proving the asymptotic normality of the estimator without necessarily assuming finite variance for the underlying process. A multiplier bootstrap methodology is suggested for obtaining a consistent estimator of the variance for this new estimator. Empirical evidence favoring this approach is provided.

papers.title: Contextuality analysis of disturbing data cannot preserve core Kochen-Specker principles
papers.abstract: We address the challenge of extending the criterion for Kochen-Specker contextuality to data with disturbance, to accommodate experimental imperfections or applications to macroscopic settings beyond quantum physics. We find that any such extension must abandon one or more principles that are core to the concept of contextuality. Specifically, we prove that no extended criterion agreeing with Kochen-Specker contextuality in the absence of disturbance can simultaneously satisfy the following: (1) any deterministic system is noncontextual; (2) discarding information cannot turn a noncontextual system into a contextual one; (3) classical post-processing cannot create contextuality; and (4) the joint realization of two statistically independent noncontextual systems is noncontextual. From the standpoint of resource theories, the obstruction arises because free operations can turn noncontextual disturbing behaviors into contextual non-disturbing ones. We suggest that future work on extended contextuality needs to move beyond the standard model-independent framework and account for the causal structure responsible for disturbance.

papers.title: Accelerated Nonnegative Tensor Completion via Integer Programming
papers.abstract: The problem of tensor completion has applications in healthcare, computer vision, and other domains. However, past approaches to tensor completion have faced a tension in that they either have polynomial-time computation but require exponentially more samples than the information-theoretic rate, or they use fewer samples but require solving NP-hard problems for which there are no known practical algorithms. A recent approach, based on integer programming, resolves this tension for nonnegative tensor completion. It achieves the information-theoretic sample complexity rate and deploys the Blended Conditional Gradients algorithm, which requires a linear (in numerical tolerance) number of oracle steps to converge to the global optimum. The tradeoff in this approach is that, in the worst case, the oracle step requires solving an integer linear program. Despite this theoretical limitation, numerical experiments show that this algorithm can, on certain instances, scale up to 100 million entries while running on a personal computer. The goal of this paper is to further enhance this algorithm, with the intention to expand both the breadth and scale of instances that can be solved. We explore several variants that can maintain the same theoretical guarantees as the algorithm, but offer potentially faster computation. We consider different data structures, acceleration of gradient descent steps, and the use of the Blended Pairwise Conditional Gradients algorithm. We describe the original approach and these variants, and conduct numerical experiments in order to explore various tradeoffs in these algorithmic design choices.

papers.title: Sketching for First Order Method: Efficient Algorithm for Low-Bandwidth Channel and Vulnerability
papers.abstract: Sketching, which randomly compresses a large problem into lower dimensions to save runtime and memory, is a fundamental tool in large-scale machine learning. We propose a sketching scheme for first order methods in distributed learning that reduces the communication cost per round between agents, keeps our bound on the total communication no larger than for uncompressed distributed gradient descent, and still guarantees convergence. An agent compresses a gradient of high dimension $d$ with a sketching matrix $R\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times d}$, $s\ll d$, and the receiver maps it back to dimension $d$ with the de-sketching matrix $R^\top$. Using this framework, we develop federated learning algorithms with lower per-round communication. However, such random sketching alone gives no formal privacy guarantee for the local data. We present a gradient-matching attack and prove that, under smoothness and non-degeneracy assumptions on the model, gradient descent on the data finds an input whose sketched gradient matches the observed one, at a linear rate. This input need not be the data, but an attacker that follows a client over several rounds with fresh sketches recovers the data with the same attack, under smoothness and non-degeneracy conditions, and no attack does so from the first $T<m/s$ rounds, where $m$ is the data dimension. As a remedy, we prove that adding Gaussian noise to the gradients makes the algorithm differentially private. This noisy variant still sends only $s$ numbers per client in each round, and for convex and strongly convex objectives it converges at the rates of the noise-free algorithm, up to an additive error term that depends on the privacy level and, in our bounds, grows as $s$ decreases. Our total communication guarantees are proved for the noise-free algorithm. We expect our sketching scheme to extend to other learning settings, and it may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Dynamic Tensor Product Regression
papers.abstract: In this work, we initiate the study of Dynamic Tensor Product Regression. One has matrices $A_1\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times d_1},\ldots,A_q\in \mathbb{R}^{n_q\times d_q}$ and a label vector $b\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\ldots n_q}$, and the goal is to solve the regression problem with the design matrix $A$ being the tensor product of the matrices $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_q$ i.e. $\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\ldots d_q}} \|(A_1\otimes \ldots\otimes A_q)x-b\|_2$. At each time step, one matrix $A_i$ receives a sparse change, and the goal is to maintain a sketch of the tensor product $A_1\otimes\ldots \otimes A_q$ so that the regression solution can be updated quickly. Recomputing the solution from scratch for each round is very slow and so it is important to develop algorithms which can quickly update the solution with the new design matrix. Our main result is a dynamic tree data structure where any update to a single matrix can be propagated quickly throughout the tree. We show that our data structure can be used to solve dynamic versions of not only Tensor Product Regression, but also Tensor Product Spline regression (which is a generalization of ridge regression) and for maintaining Low Rank Approximations for the tensor product.

papers.title: Exact Average Consensus over Unreliable Directed Networks with HARQ Feedback: Almost-Sure Convergence and Rate Characterization
papers.abstract: We study discrete-time average consensus over strongly connected directed networks with unreliable communication links, where packet errors trigger Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (HARQ) retransmissions and packets are permanently dropped after a finite retransmission limit. We propose a HARQ-based ratio-consensus algorithm that exploits ACK/NACK feedback to explicitly account for successfully delivered, delayed, and eventually dropped information mass, thereby preserving the exact network-wide average despite asymmetric communication and packet losses. To model the dependence induced by HARQ combining, we describe retransmission errors through conditional decoding-failure probabilities where we simply require the conditional probability of successful transmission to be uniformly bounded away from zero. We construct an augmented sample-path representation of the resulting delayed and dropped information flows and establish its exact equivalence with the proposed distributed iterations at the actual network nodes. Using this representation, we prove that all node ratios converge almost surely to the exact arithmetic average of the initial values. Beyond asymptotic convergence, we derive an explicit geometric bound on the expected consensus error, a high-probability error bound, and a finite upper bound on the expected time required to reach a prescribed consensus accuracy. Numerical experiments illustrate the effect of the channel reliability, HARQ combining gain, and retransmission limit on the convergence-communication trade-off, and compare the proposed method with existing robust ratio-consensus schemes.

papers.title: A geometrically intrinsic Lagrangian-Eulerian scheme for 2D Shallow Water Equations with variable topography and discontinuous data
papers.abstract: We present a Lagrangian-Eulerian scheme to solve the shallow water equations in the case of spatially variable bottom geometry. Using a local curvilinear reference system anchored on the bottom surface, we develop an effective first-order and high-resolution space-time discretization of the no-flow surfaces and solve a Lagrangian initial value problem that describes the evolution of the balance laws governing the geometrically intrinsic shallow water equations. The evolved solution set is then projected back to the original surface grid to complete the proposed Lagrangian-Eulerian formulation. The resulting scheme maintains monotonicity and captures shocks without providing excessive numerical dissipation also in the presence of non-autonomous fluxes such as those arising from the geometrically intrinsic shallow water equation on variable topographies. We provide a representative set of numerical examples to illustrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed Lagrangian-Eulerian formulation for two-dimensional surfaces with general curvatures and discontinuous initial conditions.

papers.title: Marked Persistent Homology: Circuits and Bordisms
papers.abstract: The barcode of a persistence module does not determine the relations among prescribed cycles. We encode these relations by a filtration of kernels in fixed coordinates, whose circuits can ramify into overlapping families and later recombine, unlike the merge-tree structure of degree-zero persistence. The kernels recover the marked image module and admit simultaneous rational bordism realizations. An explicit planar Vietoris-Rips filtration exhibits the circuit changes and their surface fillings.

papers.title: Convolutions of Goss and Pellarin $L$-series
papers.abstract: We establish special value results of convolutions of Goss and Pellarin $L$-series attached to Drinfeld modules that take values in Tate algebras. Applying the class module formula of Demeslay to certain rigid analytic twists of one Drinfeld module by another, we extend the special value formula for the Pellarin $L$-function associated to the Carlitz module and the Anderson-Thakur function to Drinfeld modules of arbitrary rank and their rigid analytic trivializations. By way of the theory of Schur polynomials these identities take the form of specializations of convolutions of Rankin-Selberg type. These convolution $L$-series are also identified with covolumes of Stark units.

papers.title: Externally Valid Policy Choice
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating personalized treatment policies that are "externally valid" or "generalizable": they perform well in target populations that differ from the experimental (or training) population from which the data are sampled. We first show that welfare-maximizing policies for the experimental population are robust to a certain class of shifts in the distribution of potential outcomes between the experimental and target populations (holding characteristics fixed). We then develop methods for estimating policies that are robust to shifts in the joint distribution of outcomes and characteristics. In doing so, we highlight how treatment effect heterogeneity within the experimental population shapes external validity.

papers.title: Prospects for studies of $D^{*0} \to μ^+μ^-$ and $B_{(s)}^{*0} \to μ^+μ^-$ decays
papers.abstract: Weak decays of the vector $D^{*0}$ and $B_{(s)}^{*0}$ mesons to the $\mumu$ final state provide novel potential to test the Standard Model of particle physics. Such processes have extremely small branching fractions as the vector mesons are able to decay through electromagnetic and (for the $D^{*0}$ meson) strong interactions. Nonetheless, the production of copious quantities of these particles in LHC collisions, and the ability to exploit experimental techniques that can suppress background to low levels, provides good potential to reach interesting sensitivity. The possibility to reconstruct these processes as part of the decay chain of $B^-$ or $B_c^+$ mesons appears particularly attractive due to the clean experimental signature of the displaced vertex. Indeed, published LHCb data on $\Bm \to \pim\mumu$ decays already implies a stringent limit on the branching fraction of $D^{*0} \to μ^+μ^-$. Estimates are made on the achievable sensitivity to $D^{*0} \to μ^+μ^-$ and $B_{(s)}^{*0} \to μ^+μ^-$ decays with the LHCb experiment.

papers.title: A note on mean field games of controls with state constraints: existence of mild solutions
papers.abstract: We show the existence of mild solutions for a first-order mean field game of controls under the state constraint that trajectories be confined in a closed and bounded set in euclidean space. This extends the results of Cannarsa and Capuani to the case of a mean field game of controls. Our controls are velocities and we find that the existence of an equilibrium is complicated by the requirement that they should have enough regularity. We solve this by imposing a small Lipschitz constant on the dependence of the Lagrangian on the joint measure of states and controls.

papers.title: Strict lax algebra bundles and coherent descent
papers.abstract: Fix coprime integers $k\geq1$ and $l\geq2$, and put $D=M_k\otimes M_{l^\infty}$. Let ${\mathcal C}_{k,l}$ be the topological category with objects $M_{kl^n}$, $n\geq0$, and unital $*$-embeddings as morphisms. Adjoining $D$ as an object and applying topological Quillen Theorem~A gives a weak equivalence $|N{\mathcal C}_{k,l}|\simeq B{\rm Aut}(D)$. On finite CW complexes this space classifies normalized strict lax algebra bundles modulo morphisms, refinement, and concordance. The proof realizes strict diagrams as nested matrix subalgebras of locally trivial $D$-bundles. We show that an $M_k$-bundle embeds in a trivial $M_{kl^N}$-bundle for some $N$ if and only if its stabilization by $M_{l^\infty}$ is trivial. The same classifying space describes Segal-space cover diagrams on finite CW complexes up to paths, specified refinements, and concordance, as well as Čech descent after groupoid completion. A triangulated cylinder realizes equality of completed classes by a concordance of cover diagrams. We compute the homotopy groups of the classifying space and, for $k>1$, exhibit a class outside the image of every allowed finite rank.

papers.title: The linear Boltzmann equation in column experiments of porous media
papers.abstract: The use of the linear Boltzmann equation is proposed for transport in porous media in a column. By column experiments, we show that the breakthrough curve is reproduced by the linear Boltzmann equation. The advection-diffusion equation is derived from the linear Boltzmann equation in the asymptotic limit of large propagation distance and long time.

papers.title: A Survey of Miss-Ratio Curve Construction Techniques
papers.abstract: Miss ratio curve (MRC), or equivalently hit ratio curve (HRC), construction techniques have gathered the attention of many researchers. Advances in sampling now allow these curves to be approximated in constant space, which makes online working-set-size (WSS) measurement practical. Techniques span the algorithmic design paradigm from classic stack processing to compiler analysis and machine learning. Our survey produces a broad classification of the techniques based primarily on \emph{what} locality metric is recorded and \emph{how} that metric is stored for processing. Applications of these curves span from dynamic cache partitioning in the processor, to slab allocation in key-value caches, to memory tiering at the operating system level. Our survey gives an overview of the historical, exact MRC construction methods, and compares them with the state-of-the-art methods present in today's literature. This revised version improves our coverage of existing techniques and adds the techniques published since 2017 (including methods for non-LRU and multi-tier caches), the unification of the reuse time models, and a short introduction to writeback ratio curves. Finally, we revisit the open problems posed in the first version and show where there are still open areas of research.

papers.title: Regularity for Infinitely Degenerate Inhomogeneous Elliptic Equations, Part II: A Lower Half-Harnack Inequality and Continuity
papers.abstract: We prove continuity of weak solutions to inhomogeneous quasilinear infinitely degenerate elliptic equations. Under abstract assumptions on the degenerate geometry: an Orlicz-Sobolev inequality with a super-radius, a (1,1)-Poincare inequality, a growth condition relating the super-radius to the rate at which the measure of the metric balls decays, and a Dini condition on the right hand side. The proof combines the upper bounds for negative powers of super solutions obtained in Part I with a Bombieri-Giusti lemma to obtain a lower Harnack inequality with an explicit radius-dependent constant. A measure-to-pointwise lemma in the spirit of De Giorgi then yields an oscillation estimate, which can be iterated because the growth condition keeps the accumulated constants under control. No upper half-Harnack inequality is needed. We apply the new results to obtain C^2 continuity for C^{1,1} solutions to infinitely degenerate Monge-Ampere equations in two dimensions.

papers.title: Collatz meets Fibonacci
papers.abstract: The Collatz map is defined for a positive even integer as half that integer, and for a positive odd integer as that integer threefold, plus one. The Collatz conjecture states that when the map is iterated the number one is eventually reached. We study permutations that arise as sequences from this iteration. We show that permutations of this type of length up to 14 are enumerated by the Fibonacci numbers. Beyond that excess permutations appear. We will explain the appearance of these excess permutations and give an upper bound on the exact enumeration.

papers.title: A unification of permutation patterns related to Schubert varieties
papers.abstract: We obtain new connections between permutation patterns and singularities of Schubert varieties, by giving a new characterization of Gorenstein varieties in terms of so called bivincular patterns. These are generalizations of classical patterns where conditions are placed on the location of an occurrence in a permutation, as well as on the values in the occurrence. This clarifies what happens when the requirement of smoothness is weakened to factoriality and further to Gorensteinness, extending work of Bousquet-Melou and Butler (2007), and Woo and Yong (2006). We also show how mesh patterns, introduced by Branden and Claesson (2011), subsume many other types of patterns and define an extension of them called marked mesh patterns. We use these new patterns to further simplify the description of Gorenstein Schubert varieties and give a new description of Schubert varieties that are defined by inclusions, introduced by Gasharov and Reiner (2002). We also give a description of 123-hexagon avoiding permutations, introduced by Billey and Warrington (2001), Dumont permutations and cycles in terms of marked mesh patterns.

papers.title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
papers.abstract: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance. Recovering these intrinsics from images is ambiguous, and methods that predict them per pixel give the same surface point a different decomposition in every view. We introduce PointX, a simple feed-forward model that predicts intrinsics per 3D surface point instead. A multi-view transformer encodes a set of unposed images, and for any queried surface point, PointX pools the point's tokens across the views in which it appears and decodes the point's intrinsics once. Each point of a 3D reconstruction of the scene, such as a point cloud or a mesh, thus receives a single prediction, which is exactly consistent across views by construction and enables view-consistent relighting and editing. The same model also predicts per-view maps, from one image or many, by querying the point seen at every pixel. These maps agree across views up to the precision of the estimated geometry and correspondences. PointX is significantly more consistent than existing methods, while remaining competitive in accuracy from a single image and improving as views are added. Project page: https://pointx-paper.github.io/

papers.title: Antiferromagnetic phase of MnTe2: spin-order-induced renormalization of phonon Raman spectrum
papers.abstract: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the Néel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. It has been found that below the magnetic transition temperature, the frequencies of four out of five Raman-active lattice vibrations (i.e., Eg and three Tg phonon modes) revealed significant departure from the mechanism of the three-phonon anharmonic decay described by Klemens model. Here, we propose a new model considering spin-phonon coupling to explain frequency renormalization of the phonon part of the Raman spectrum upon the para-/antiferro- (PM/AFM) magnetic phase transition change in MnTe2. Through employing Green's function formalism, we show that a simple two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet approach follows well both spin ordering induced hardening and softening of phonon modes observed in AFM phase of MnTe2 upon cooling. Additionally, the detailed temperature and field dependences of the energy for both magnon modes are presented. In addition to unexpected twofold anisotropy of the higher energy magnon mode (approx. 3.5 meV) unveiled in crossed configuration, our magneto-optical measurements revealed a subtle, yet definite softening trend for the lower energy mode (approx. 2.6 meV). Although the precise reasons for these effects remain unclear, we put forward a symmetry reduction in the local atomic surroundings as a possible mechanism for discussion.

papers.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
papers.abstract: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpiński carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpiński carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].

papers.title: Dominoes tiling a common figure
papers.abstract: Call a two-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a domino. Given finitely many dominoes $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, we show that there exists a finite non-empty $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $B$ can be partitioned into disjoint translates of $D_i$ for all $i$. The proof uses a new absorption mechanism for perfect matchings in algebraically defined hypergraphs.

papers.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
papers.abstract: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. On DiaDemBench, which we extend with utterance-level timestamps and subtitle redaction, both DiaCap with off-the-shelf transcripts and its end-to-end variant DiaCap-E2E achieve strong results. Specifically, DiaCap performs on par with Gemini 4 Argon in audiovisual diarization while clearly outperforming it in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs. 42.76 TIME). It also maintains strong diarization on multilingual and minute-long videos, and transfers to audiovisual question answering.

papers.title: Abelian envelopes and quantum groups in Knop's interpolation categories
papers.abstract: We show the existence of abelian envelopes for large classes of subcategories of Knop's tensor envelopes. It follows that these abelian envelopes correspond to groups or more generally Hopf algebras (``quantum groups'') in their parent interpolation categories. As a special case, we obtain that the interpolation categories in the sense of Flake--Maassen (2022) of all so-called group-theoretical easy quantum groups have abelian envelopes given by quantum groups in Deligne's interpolation category of the symmetric groups. Similarly, we apply our theory to interpolation categories of wreath products, finite general linear groups, and finite affine groups. Our main technique is an explicit construction of objects corresponding to coordinate algebras using the calculus of relations that Knop's categories are based on.

papers.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
papers.abstract: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision. We preserve exact image-text matches while introducing weaker positive supervision for related pairs, such as a panel and the caption of a sibling panel. We upweight cross-article negatives of the same content type to encourage finer discrimination. We also enrich panel descriptions using visual content, original figure captions, and mentioning paragraphs. Pairing panels with these descriptions and whole figures with their original captions yields Loom52M, a dataset of 52.4 million image-text pairs spanning scientific charts and biomedical images. Using Loom52M, BioLoom (DFN-2B) achieves 56.82% domain-balanced mean accuracy across 67 zero-shot classification tasks from 43 datasets in 10 domains, compared with 48.77% for MedPMC-CLIP. On BioLoomBench with concise captions and BioMedFlickr, it achieves bidirectional mean Recall@1 of 63.20% and 10.59%, versus 46.37% and 7.55% for the respective strongest evaluated baselines, BiomedCLIP and MedPMC-CLIP. Code, datasets, benchmarks, and models are available at https://bioloom-clip.github.io/.

papers.title: Parametric neural-network wavefunctions across a bosonic phase transition
papers.abstract: We propose Boseformer, a universal attention-based neural-network architecture for representing the wavefunctions of particles with bosonic quantum statistics, including superfluid and crystal phases. The model is trained to generate the wavefunction as a function of a Hamiltonian parameter across the quantum phase transition between these phases. Once trained with variational Monte Carlo optimization, it can serve as a foundation model describing the phase transition without the need to retrain it for individual parameter values. We demonstrate our method on a system of two-dimensional bosons with $1/r^3$ repulsive interaction.

papers.title: Envy-Free Cake-Cutting for Five Agents
papers.abstract: We study the envy-free cake-cutting problem, in which a divisible resource must be divided among a set of agents with heterogeneous preferences in a way that ensures that no agent envies the piece obtained by another. Remarkably, under some mild continuity assumptions on the agent valuations, it is known that an envy-free division where each agent receives a \emph{connected} piece of the cake is always guaranteed to exist. When the valuations are monotone, prior work has shown that a connected $\varepsilon$-envy-free division can be obtained using $\poly(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries for up to four agents, leaving the case of five or more agents open. In this work, we develop a new simpler approach that yields such an efficient algorithm for five agents. Our algorithm uses $\mathcal{O}(\log^3(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and also yields a novel proof of existence for five agents that does not rely on any fixed-point theorems beyond the intermediate value theorem.

papers.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
papers.abstract: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. The standard fine-tuning approach imitates both, yet the strongest teachers are closed models whose chain-of-thought is hidden behind an API. We show that the chain-of-thought can be left out altogether and that the long-horizon policy can be distilled from the teacher's actions alone. The student is trained on these trajectories with its reasoning block left empty, while a KL loss on a replay buffer of its own generations limits drift from its initial model. Surprisingly, the policy learned from these trajectories with an empty reasoning block carries over to inference with thinking enabled, where the student reasons in its own style while acting like the teacher, an effect we call cross-format transfer. Distilling the actions of Qwen3.6-27B raises the task success of Qwen3-4B on AppWorld from 7% to 18% and that of Qwen3-32B from 12% to 25%. We further introduce CoT-proxies, short summaries of the teacher's reasoning placed after the empty reasoning block, which raise Qwen3-4B further, to 35%. Since neither actions nor CoT-proxies need the hidden chain-of-thought, the recipe applies unchanged to closed teachers. Distilling GPT-5.6 Luna from its visible outputs and the reasoning summaries its API returns raises Qwen3-4B from 7% to 48% on AppWorld and from 3% to 28% on SWE-bench Verified.

papers.title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
papers.abstract: Creating a dialogue scene typically requires cutting between multiple views (e.g., close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder shots) of the actors. Yet capturing such coverage is costly and in many settings unavailable. We study dialogue re-cinematography: synthesizing additional shots from a single wide-angle dialogue video. Existing video generators can synthesize new shots, but rely on visual cues alone, so when the source video barely shows the lips, the generated lip motion fails to match the speech. Our key observation is that the speech audio is view-invariant: it constrains lip motion in any target view. Building on this insight, we adapt a pretrained audio-visual diffusion model to generate the new shot from a target frame that specifies the view, a source video that contains the performance, and the speech audio that drives lip motion. In multi-person scenes, however, pretrained audio-visual models drive every visible face with the same speech, causing speech leakage, where silent listeners mouth the speaker's words. We therefore introduce speaker-aware audio gating, a training-free module that lets the audio drive only the faces that speak in the target shot. On a cinematic paired-view benchmark spanning diverse viewpoints and framings, our method lowers perceptual error by 59%, landmark error by 56%, and speech leakage by 97% relative to the strongest baseline, Wan 3.0. Our method also remains robust on in-the-wild scenes, highlighting its potential for film post-production.

papers.title: The double copy and perturbative teleparallel gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper we analyze the double copy between gluon and graviton amplitudes within the context of teleparallel gravity. We first set up an effective Lagrangian based on minimal assumptions which reproduces the on-shell amplitudes stemming from the double-copy procedure. By straightforwardly computing the three- and four-point amplitude, this double-copy Lagrangian can be constrained up to a few real parameters when expanding to quartic order. For a specific choice of parameters, we find an exact equivalence with perturbative teleparallel gravity. This suggests that the teleparallel formulation might be well suited to make the double copy more transparent from a Lagrangian viewpoint.

papers.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
papers.abstract: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild. In light of this, we present Lost on Campus, a benchmark for evaluating ESR in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our benchmark introduces a unified reasoning-action evaluation framework that seamlessly integrates diagnostic QA for isolated reasoning with closed-loop interactive navigation for active reasoning under multimodal instructions. To enable fine-grained diagnosis, we evaluate six capability aspects of ESR: action grounding, spatial foresight, metric awareness, goal-directed planning, ego-allocentric localization, and spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments reveal that: (i) Compared to indoor settings, real-world outdoor environments impose substantially higher demands on spatial reasoning, where existing models exhibit poor performance; (ii) VLMs still struggle with fine-grained visual alignment, with failures in spatial foresight and ego-allocentric localization emerging as primary bottlenecks; (iii) Improving multimodal interaction capabilities and long-term spatial reasoning is crucial for advancing embodied intelligence. These findings highlight that faithful evaluation of ESR demands benchmarks tightly coupling perception, reasoning and action within realistic and continuous environments.

papers.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.

papers.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
papers.abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement. It comprises 250 manually validated tasks across 11 types in five groups and 27 indoor environments, covering object and room search, counting, geometric judgments, direction reasoning, and relocation. Human evaluators achieve 84% strict task success on 100 sampled tasks, with every correct outcome satisfying the required checks. Across seven frontier vision-language models, we identify two complementary failure modes: correct outcomes with unmet task requirements, and incorrect outcomes despite passing stronger checks. Oracle-input diagnostics show that more complete target observations and calibrated feedback improve final spatial judgments.

papers.title: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey
papers.abstract: We present strong-lensing models for the 57 galaxy clusters observed in Cycle 4 out of the 60 targeted by the JWST Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS) program. Models for the remaining three clusters will be incorporated after their observations. The dataset comprises 5013 individual images, corresponding to 1733 multiply-imaged systems, of which 912 have spectroscopic redshift measurements and 227 are newly identified. Using this new wealth of observations, we construct parametric lens models with our $\mathtt{AstroLensPy}$ software, reproducing the observed image positions with an average image-plane precision $Δ_{\rm RMS}$ of $0.54''$. With a total imaging area of $576$ arcmin$^2$, VENUS offers the largest homogeneous set of cluster strong-lensing models to date. The clusters yield a combined area of $191$ arcmin$^{2}$ magnified by $|μ|\geq3$ for a source $z_s=10$, for example, establishing the VENUS fields as a premier survey for high-redshift studies. Among our sample, the clusters MACS J0717.5+3745, RXC J0600.1-2007 and PLCK G287.0+32.9 display the largest Einstein radii ($\geq 60''$) and magnified areas ($\mathcal{A}_{z_s=10}^{|μ|\geq3} \geq 9$ arcmin$^2$) for a source $z_s=10$, and therefore constitute the most potent gravitational telescopes known to date. Finally, leveraging the statistical power of the sample, we derive scaling relations between various lensing observables (Einstein radius, magnified area, projected mass) and the SZ/X-ray-inferred cluster mass, $M_{500,c}$.

papers.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. This motivates efficient proxies for future imagination, but how to train such proxies without sacrificing action-prediction quality remains unclear. An effective proxy need not generate a high-resolution frame; it only needs to provide enough information to distinguish between possible futures. This leads to the design principle behind iWAM: rather than denoising an entire future frame, can we condition the action policy on intermediate features from a single video-model evaluation? We show that the answer is yes. Exploiting the reversible dynamics of flow-matching models, we invert each training future into the corresponding latent noise vector. However, a single velocity evaluation at this latent does not necessarily yield informative features for action prediction. We therefore learn a bidirectional flow map that amortizes future-generation computation, enabling a single model evaluation to provide effective conditioning features. At inference, we sample a latent noise vector from the prior and condition the policy using just one video-backbone forward pass. Across simulated benchmarks and real robots, iWAM recovers the generalization benefits of WAMs while substantially reducing its inference cost.

papers.title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
papers.abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.

papers.title: On Euclidean Diameter in Dynamic Streams
papers.abstract: We give a streaming algorithm for maintaining the diameter of a high-dimensional Euclidean point set under arbitrary insertions and deletions that achieves update time polylogarithmic in the number of points and polynomial in the dimension. For every fixed $c>\sqrt3$, there is an $ε_c > 0$ such that our one-pass algorithm uses $\tilde O(N^{1-ε_c}\poly(d))$ space, has worst-case update time $\poly(d,\log N)$, and maintains a factor-$c$ pair witness. On the hardness side, we prove that every constant-factor approximation requires polynomial memory even on short dynamic streams: a factor-$c$ approximation needs $N^{Ω(1/(c^2\log(c+1)))}$ space on streams of at most $2N-1$ updates. Our upper bound combines a geometric hull, Gaussian hashing through successively smaller caps, and local and global rebuilding schedules. Every update changes only one leaf of the hash hierarchy, while the answer is maintained through small variance certificates. The lower bound is based on a communication complexity argument. Together, these results separate the polynomial memory regime from the time needed to process an update.

papers.title: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions
papers.abstract: The variational quantum algorithm ADAPT-VQE has previously been used to prepare the vacuum of lattice gauge theories in $1+1D$. In this paper, we study whether it extends to higher dimensions. We identify two general limitations of ADAPT-VQE. First, if the qubit Hamiltonian and the initial state are real, i.e., invariant under qubit-level time-reversal, all real-valued pool operators have vanishing gradients and are never selected. Second, the algorithm can converge to excited eigenstates. We illustrate both limitations, also providing examples from literature, and present a first application of ADAPT-VQE to a lattice field theory in $2+1D$, namely free Wilson fermions, where both obstacles occur. Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool improves the results, and combining different pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states over the full mass range. These findings give practical guidelines for applying ADAPT-VQE to lattice field theories beyond $1+1D$.

papers.title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action
papers.abstract: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning. We demonstrate its value as training data across inverse rendering, 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and mobile manipulation. Across these tasks, training state-of-the-art methods with our scenes improves performance over alternative synthetic datasets. In addition, we introduce a mobile manipulation benchmark, evaluating vision-language-action models performing physical pick and place in diverse 3D scenes with realistic layouts, and using our part annotations to also score where each object is grasped. Our dataset will be released publicly to facilitate research in visual and embodied AI.

papers.title: A canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem: for any finite set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a scaled (and possibly rotated) copy of $S$ that is either monochromatic or rainbow.

papers.title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation
papers.abstract: Language models can generate LEGO$^\circledR$ assemblies from text, but their builds often contain parts that collide or attach to nothing. The usual approach of rejecting and resampling invalid placements discards decoded tokens without guaranteeing a valid build. We present BriConstrain, a constrained decoding method that restricts a pretrained language model's next-token probabilities before sampling, steering it towards valid placements. Because the validity of a brick placement depends on the non-predetermined build state, it cannot be compiled into a fixed grammar and must be checked dynamically. However, checking the validity of a brick before sampling is challenging as the space of valid placements is combinatorially large and cannot be enumerated exhaustively. Our key idea is to narrow the search space by constraining how parts attach rather than which parts attach to each other. Concretely, given the model's predictions of the currently placed part, and the previously placed parent it wants to connect to, we constrain the model's choice of how they attach. This allows us to span the space of part attachments, using a precomputed geometric oracle, and to effectively filter out colliding options. With valid attachment candidates in hand, we bias the model's next-token distribution towards the remaining valid candidates. We evaluate our method on two LEGO$^\circledR$ formats and models: BrickNet, which annotates connectivity explicitly, and our proposed Implicit Connectivity LDraw Format (ICLF), which uses numeric values for placements and leaves connectivity implicit. Our method raises collision-free builds from 31% to 91% on BrickNet and from 15% to 65% on ICLF, and outperforms rejection sampling on both formats at about 60% of its decoding cost.

papers.title: Regenerative range for planar random walks
papers.abstract: We consider a centred random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which consumes resources originally present at every site. After consumption, each resource regenerates independently with probability $p$ at each step. We study the number of resources consumed up to time $n$, which is denoted $C_n$. Letting $p=p_n$ depend on $n$ and supposing that the walk moves faster than the resources regenerate, $i.e.$ $p_n=o(1)$, we establish a Law of Large Numbers and a Central Limit Theorem for $C_n$. In particular, we identify a phase transition between a so-called fast regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrow\infty$, where the fluctuations of $C_n$ are Gaussian, and a slow regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrowλ\in[0,\infty)$, where the fluctuations are non-Gaussian and described by a weighted renormalized self-intersection local time of planar Brownian motion depending on the parameter $λ$.

papers.title: A Bias in Disguise: Tiny Gradient Edits Stop a Small Language Model's Thinking Loops and Complement a Frontier Model's Weight Edit
papers.abstract: Qwen3.5-0.8B rarely finishes reasoning in thinking mode: at a 4,096-token budget only 1 or 2 of 500 MATH-500 answers close their think block (two seeds), and accuracy is 15.4%. A recent demonstration had GPT-6 Astra edit 131,072 of the model's weights without gradients and reported MATH-500 rising from 7.9% to 48.1% at a 32,768-token budget. We provide the missing gradient baseline, then combine the two edits. Fine-tuning only the 140 to 139,750 weights with the largest gradient, on the model's own correct answers to MATH training problems, raises thinking-mode MATH-500 at 4k tokens to 39.0-45.5% after 2-9 minutes of training on one GPU; 50 training examples suffice, and 1,398 random positions give only 16.3%. The gradient concentrates the edit on the most nearly constant channel of each of the first three layers. Because the model has no bias terms, an edit confined to those channels acts as a constant vector added to the residual stream: adding three fixed vectors to the unedited model matches the accuracy of such an edit. Under the Astra protocol (32k tokens, presence penalty 1.5), the Astra edit scores 52.1% (finished and correct) in our reproduction and our full-strength edits reach 45.6-45.7%, but ours win at every budget up to 16k tokens (39.5% against 6.7% at 4k). The two edits are complementary. The Astra edit plus our 139,750-weight edit at half strength scores 62.2% at 32k, 10 points above the Astra edit alone (p = 3e-9), with half as many tokens; our half-strength edit alone scores 46.7%.

papers.title: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8π^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperkähler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.

papers.title: Hölder continuity of Green functions for Markov sets
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb C^N$. We prove that its Green function (and consequently, the Siciak extremal function) is Hölder continuous if and only if the first derivatives of polynomials satisfy Markov's inequality on $K$. The implication from Markov's inequality to Hölder continuity of the associated Green function settles a longstanding open problem at the intersection of approximation theory and pluripotential theory. A Markov bound $An^m$ in degree $n$ gives every Hölder exponent below $1/m$. In one complex variable it gives the exponent $1/m$ itself. The proof compares the extremal functions of two neighborhoods of $K$. For $N>1$ we use Hörmander's theorem on holomorphic extension from a point. For $N=1$ the comparison follows from the maximum principle.

papers.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
papers.abstract: Robot policies predominantly learn from human-collected data emphasizing competent behavior, limiting coverage of the low-level behaviors needed to support autonomous improvement. We study how a form of midtraining can be used to build coverage over diverse low-level behaviors that connect challenging states of the robot and its environment to states from which further progress is possible ("connected behavioral coverage"). We also examine how this coverage supports downstream adaptation and online improvement. To this end, we introduce $β$-Data, a dataset collected via adversarial teleoperation, where a human adversary reversibly perturbs the environment while a human operator continues toward completion without resetting. We relabel trajectory segments with local outcomes in natural language and finetune a pretrained policy conditioned on recent action history. The resulting policy exhibits sustained use of more low-level behaviors. Across manipulation tasks in simulation and on three real-robot platforms, our approach yields more favorable data scaling laws, better zero-shot generalization, and more effective use of additional rollout time than training on standard demonstrations. During online finetuning, these policies need fewer rollouts to collect successful experience and reach higher success rates, suggesting that midtraining can prepare robots for both more robust task execution and continued autonomous improvement. Our project page and robot videos are available at https://kshitiz-1225.github.io/exploratory-midtraining-robot-policies/.

papers.title: A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression
papers.abstract: For a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, we determine when the Holevo rate is achievable with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. In the maximal Koashi--Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble, this occurs exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits, this means that the signals are all pure or commute pairwise. If any occupied quantum part is mixed, every code with sufficiently small mean local error has rate bounded away from the Holevo information, uniformly in blocklength. To prove the converse, we apply Fawzi--Renner recovery to a hypothetical sequence of visible codes approaching the Holevo rate at vanishing local error, then invoke a decoupling bound of Baghali Khanian and Winter for blind compression.

papers.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
papers.abstract: The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods. Nonetheless, theoretical evidence for or against such an advantage remains scarce. Here, we investigate this in sparse random non-local Hamiltonians. We design a classical algorithm for such Hamiltonians that enables accurate computation of spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision $\varepsilon$, our algorithm runs in time $(1/\varepsilon)^{2+o(1)}$, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. Crucially, this applies even at late evolution times, low temperatures, and near critical points, where existing classical methods require exponential time. Rather than directly simulating a quantum state or operator, our algorithm first computes the model's mean behavior and then a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections. These corrections predict long-time behavior based on short-time data using free probability theory.

papers.title: A note on input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies
papers.abstract: Unambiguous hierarchies are defined similarly to the polynomial hierarchy; however, all witnesses must be unique. Their versions differ in the mode of using oracles. We consider input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies built from the class OUP, in which all positive inputs of the same length have the same unique witness: the hierarchy OUH with language oracles and the hierarchy OUH$_\bullet$ with loose access to promise oracles, which is the input-oblivious version of the loose unambiguous hierarchy of Hirsch and Sokolov (IPL, 2015). We show that languages in OUH$_\bullet$ can be decided in deterministic polynomial time with an ONP oracle, and for languages in OUH oracle queries can be made nonadaptive. Moreover, languages in OUH can be decided in deterministic polynomial time with a tally NP oracle, and languages in OUH$_{\bullet}$ can be decided in P/OptP, that is, a subclass of P/poly where the advice is generated by a function that maximizes outputs of a nondeterministic machine on a unary input. We show that P/OptP can be characterized in terms of OGTD and OUGTD generator--tester--decoder classes recently considered by Hirsch and Volkovich (arXiv:cs.CC/2611.16096) and, in particular, is contained in their "ultimate" Karp--Lipton collapse class OUM. We also observe several other facts related to OUP: (1) the hierarchy defined by input-oblivious unambiguous dot-operators collapses, (2) in OUP computations, a single loose query to prOUP can be replaced by a query to OUP, (3) SOUP=OUP$\cap$coOUP, where SOUP is the same-witness class recently considered by Hirsch, Volkovich, and Williams (2026).

papers.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.

papers.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details. We present SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and discovers complementary evidence through query-time lexical expansion. Memory construction requires no model inference, using a lexical index without LLM-based extraction, summarization, or semantic relation construction. At query time, BM25 retrieves initial candidates, an evidence evaluator identifies useful chunks, and lexical cues from selected evidence guide an additional retrieval round. Retrieved dialogue is further annotated with calendar interpretations of supported relative-time expressions, preserving the original wording and temporal granularity. We also introduce SAG-Mem-Lite, an alternative configuration that replaces evidence scoring with embedding-based candidate scoring, achieving lower operational cost than Full Context and all memory-based baselines across both benchmarks with low query latency. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval, SAG-Mem achieves overall scores of 83.08 and 80.20, respectively, the highest among the evaluated methods on both benchmarks. On LongMemEval, it exceeds the strongest compared baseline by 7.20 points. SAG-Mem-Lite achieves scores of 77.09 and 77.20, respectively.
