The linear estimator is updated alongside the main language model, fitting to the exact gradient-based utility scores obtained from the backward pass of regular training steps. Consequently, scoring a candidate requires only a linear transformation, bypassing the costly gradient-alignment computation. We demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency for LLM pretraining in English and multilingual scenarios, with various steering target designs. The improvements from DAiSy can consistently survive the instruction-tuning phase.

papers.title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
papers.abstract: Problem-independent machine learning (PIML) is an effective computational approach that combines the finite element method with machine learning. PIML uses neural networks to learn the mapping from material distributions or element geometries to the numerical shape functions of substructures. This approach avoids repeated computation while preserving the conformity of the underlying finite element discretization, thereby significantly improving the efficiency of substructure-based finite element analysis. However, existing studies on PIML have primarily focused on numerical accuracy and computational efficiency, while rigorous theoretical analyses of its approximation errors are still limited. In this paper, we establish an error analysis framework for PIML from a classical finite element perspective, in which the numerical error is bounded in terms of the finite element discretization error and the network generalization error. Our analysis shows that, when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced, the resulting error estimate contains a learning-induced term that does not necessarily decrease under mesh refinement. To ensure convergence, we propose an improved PIML scheme with linear completeness. By using linear displacement field constraints to reconstruct the corresponding columns of the transition matrix, we ensure that the resulting numerical shape-function space contains the space of linear polynomials. We derive error estimates and establish convergence results of the improved scheme in the H1 and L2 norms. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate that the improved PIML achieves optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.

papers.title: VC-OPD: Learning to See What Matters via Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Visual On-Policy Distillation (OPD) commonly uses cropped or zoomed-in image regions as teacher-side privileged information to improve fine-grained perception in small Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). However, local pixel-level cues are insufficient for complex visual reasoning that requires global structure, spatial relationships, and high-level semantics. We propose Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation (VC-OPD), which extends teacher-side privileged information beyond local image regions to question-conditioned visual cues. Advanced MLLMs generate cues capturing key visual details, structural relationships, and semantic evidence needed to answer each question. A multi-stage quality filtering process selects reliable cues, which are provided only to the teacher during training. This enables informative token-level supervision along student-generated trajectories, helping the student learn to identify and reason over critical evidence directly from the original image. No additional information is required at inference time. Since advanced MLLMs are used only for visual cue generation, VC-OPD is compatible with both open-weight and proprietary black-box models. Experiments on STEM and general visual reasoning benchmarks show consistent improvements across model scales over reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation baselines. Notably, a 4B model trained with VC-OPD outperforms many baselines with 8B or more parameters, demonstrating effective capability transfer through question-conditioned visual cues.

papers.title: Covalent Welding of Two-Dimensional Molecular Sheets into Ultra-Stiff, Super-Tough Polymeric Networks
papers.abstract: Since the inception of macromolecular science, polymers have been constructed from zero-dimensional monomers, a paradigm that funnels all stress through discrete one-dimensional chains. Driven by conformational entropy, polymer chains inevitably coil in three-dimensional space, precluding effective stress transfer, thereby compromising the ultimate mechanical performance. Two-dimensional (2D) molecular sheets, with intrinsic in-plane rigidity, could in principle circumvent this constraint. Yet in existing assemblies, where stress transfers efficiently within each molecular sheet but poorly between them, their exceptional properties fail to translate to the macroscale. Here, we demonstrate a 2D highly oriented molecular network (2D HOMN), an ultra-stiff, super-tough polymeric material constructed by the solid-state covalent welding of assembled 2D polyaramid sheets with flexible linkers pre-grafted at their peripheries. Enabled by efficient intersheet load sharing and energy dissipation, the welded films rival the modulus and strength of Kevlar 29 fibers, reaching 69.8 and 3.9 GPa, with impact toughness up to an order of magnitude beyond Kevlar composites. This designed intersheet covalent connectivity further renders the 2D HOMN impermeable to gas molecules and ions, resilient to radiation and efficient in thermal transport. This work establishes 2D molecular motifs as heterogeneous monomeric building blocks and provides a general strategy for constructing multifunctional polymeric networks.

papers.title: $ε$-Seg++: Ensembling Across Hierarchy and Training Time for Label-Efficient EM Segmentation
papers.abstract: Semantic segmentation of electron microscopy (EM) volumes is a central step in quantitative cell biology, but dense voxel-wise annotation is prohibitively expensive. $ε$-Seg showed that a hierarchical variational autoencoder trained on sparsely annotated voxels can yield competitive segmentations, but it classifies from its topmost latent level only and operates exclusively on 2D patches. We introduce $ε$-Seg++, which places a semantic expert at every level of the hierarchy and consolidates their predictions with a parameter-free product of experts. We further enable 3D inputs through a leakage-free sub-volume splitting protocol, which allows 2D and 3D models to be compared under identical sparse supervision. Because validation labels are just as scarce as training labels, we treat checkpoint selection as part of the method and average the top-ranked checkpoints, a second ensemble, this time across training time. On the BetaSeg FIB-SEM dataset, the multi-level experts improve 2D mean Dice by about 0.1 at 2,500 training labels. With up to 600 training labels, the 2D model matches or exceeds 3D $ε$-Seg at about one eleventh of its prediction cost. Above roughly a thousand labels, 3D inputs dominate, and at matched annotation cost 3D $ε$-Seg++ reaches a mean Dice of 0.905 versus 0.880 for D3PM, while predicting between 5.4 and 27 times faster (with our checkpoint ensemble or a single model, respectively). Checkpoint ensembling matches single-best selection on average and markedly improves the worst case when the validation set is small.

papers.title: Perturbation of CO A1Π by a3Π should have been undetectable: detection, mechanism, and surprises
papers.abstract: A direct perturbation between the $a^3Π$ and $A^1Π$ vibrational levels of two electronic states that belong to the same electronic configuration of the carbon monoxide molecule should be unobservably weak because the vibrational overlap integral $\langle a^3Π,v' \mid A^1Π,v'' \rangle$ for their near-degenerate levels is extremely small. Yet level-shift and transition-intensity signatures of the $a^3Π(v = 13) \sim A^1Π(v = 2)$ perturbation are unmistakably present in the $^{13}\mathrm{C}^{18}\mathrm{O}$ isotopologue. A detailed study of, among others, the $A^1Π$ - $X^1Σ^+(2, 0)$, $B^1Σ^+$ - $A^1Π(0, 2)$, and $C^1Σ^+$ - $A^1Π(0, 2)$ spectra, obtained by the VUV- and Vis-FT complementary techniques in the energy regions of the six crossing points ($e$- and $f$-symmetry, $|Ω| = 0, 1, 2$) between the $a^3Π(v = 13)$ and $A^1Π(v = 2)$ states, reveal that the perturbation pathways are indirect, primarily facilitated by the $e^3Σ^-(v = 4)$ state, and that quantum mechanical interferences via its F1e and F3e components occur.

papers.title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
papers.abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

papers.title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
papers.abstract: Qwen3-Omni speaks through a Talker predicting 16 codebooks of a 12.5 Hz audio codec, but the encoder that made its training labels was not released, so new voices cannot be trained on matching labels. We identify this encoder from the released model's behavior. White-box regression shows that the codebook embeddings of the Talker, its multi-token predictor and the Code2Wav decoder match the first 16 codebooks of kyutai's Mimi layer by layer. A decoder-based test looks convincing but fails calibration: decoders trained on known labels cannot tell them apart. Teacher-forced Talker likelihoods, calibrated with 13 code language models trained on known labels, do tell implementations apart: the Talker prefers labels from kyutai's moshi package with bf16 weights over every other variant we tried. Loudness normalization and band-limiting of 20% or more of the data are ruled out. Separately, transformers' MimiModel encodes the last frame differently from kyutai's encoder unless the input length is a multiple of 1920 samples. After LoRA fine-tuning on its labels, 44--55% of generated sentences end in a noise burst, and the same frame costs the Mimi-based CSM-1B 119 nats; padding the input removes both. We release the encoding recipe, a label checker and a Talker fine-tuning toolkit.

papers.title: SofaSpace: A Benchmark for Executable Visual Spatial Reasoning in Continuous Motion and Environment Construction
papers.abstract: A rigid body can fit at its start and goal yet collide with a wall as it moves between them. Inspired by the moving sofa problem, we introduce SofaSpace, a benchmark for visual spatial reasoning through continuous planar rigid-body transport and environment construction. SofaSpace contains 3,000 scenes organized around three challenges: geometric compatibility, nonlocal maneuver planning, and interactive and temporal coordination. Four task views ask models to plan a motion, reconstruct a layout, design an environment that meets transport requirements, or jointly generate a layout and a motion. A separate set of 534 SofaSpace-Hard tasks tests planning and judgment. A geometric verifier checks the entire body throughout each submitted motion. On static planning tasks, endpoint agreement and continuous validity differ substantially within the same submitted plans: Claude drops from 97.2% to 52.8%, DeepSeek from 100.0% to 30.6%, and Kimi from 97.2% to 29.4%, while the strongest configuration retains 98.3% full validity. Environment construction reveals a further gap. Of 295 feasible layouts generated by the strongest configuration, 181 satisfy all evaluated functional requirements; for Kimi, one of 172 does. These results show how executable checks distinguish endpoint agreement from valid motion and geometric feasibility from functional compliance.

papers.title: Harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms and deformations of branched covers of special Lagrangians
papers.abstract: This article introduces the notion of a non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-form on a manifold $X$ in terms of immersed submanifolds of $T^*X$ and develops a deformation theory extending Donaldson's work on harmonic non-degenerate $\mathbf{Z}/2\mathbf{Z}$ $1$-forms. More precisely, the universal moduli space of harmonic non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-forms is shown to be a tame Fréchet orbifold whose projection onto the space of Riemannian metrics is a submersion and whose fibres are locally parametrised by their periods. The proof relies on Hörmander's subelliptic estimates and the Nash--Moser submersion theorem. As an application of this analytic framework, harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms on a special Lagrangian are shown to control deformations of its branched covers, extending work of He for multiplicity two.

papers.title: Exact Mass Multipoles of Distorted Schwarzschild Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Using the isolated-horizon framework, we compute the geometric and mass multipole moments of the Weyl-distorted Schwarzschild horizon without linearizing the distortion. Starting from the exact integral representation we evaluate it in closed form for two cases, a pure quadrupole distortion and a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion. For a pure quadrupole we obtain a closed form for all $\ell$ in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, while for a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion we derive a closed-form series solution in the odd-parity coefficient $β$ whose coefficients are exact in the quadrupole coefficient $α_{2}$. We use these results to understand the errors incurred by leading-order approximations. Leading-order approximations in $α_{2}$ misestimate every dimensionless mass multipole by a relative error of roughly $α_{2}$, nearly independent of $\ell$, and for pure linearization most of the error lies in the linearized quadrupole moment rather than the discarded higher multipoles. A simple degree-counting rule determines which orders of distortion contribute to each multipole. As a consequence, the odd-parity component must be small compared with $α_{2}^2$ before it can be neglected. Finally, truncating the series in $β$ at its first $β$-dependent order reproduces the $\ell \leq 6$ multipoles to about $10^{-3}$ for $|β|,|α_{2}| \leq 1/8$.

papers.title: Assessing the total mass of the Planck protocluster candidates with CMB lensing stacking
papers.abstract: Galaxy clusters in formation, or protoclusters, are important sites regarding the evolution of large scale structures and the star formation history of the Universe. With a few exceptions, only their member galaxies have been routinely observed so far. The majority of their mass is expected to be under the form of non baryonic dark matter and cold intergalactic gas. The Planck high redshift star-forming field sample compiles 2151 protocluster candidates, among which 1012 fall within the footprint of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). The lensing of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) by foreground structures allows us to try and assess the total mass of these protoclusters for the first time. We stack the CMB lensing data from ACT at the location of the Planck protocluster candidates to obtain a mean convergence signal. We then provide an estimate for the mean mass along the line of sight for these objects. The centre of the stacked field corresponds to a lensing signal at a $12\,σ$ significance level. The integration of the mass along the line of sight yields a value of $(6.6\pm 1.4) \times 10^{14}\,M_\odot$, similar to what is expected from numerical simulations. With the constraint $1.5 < z < 3$ from Planck, we are able to rule out the possibility that this sample is populated by virialised massive structures. This is the first time that the mass of Planck high redshift sources is measured in such a direct way. The results we obtain constitute a new strong argument in favour of this sample being composed of a majority of galaxy protoclusters lying at $z \geq 1$.

papers.title: StreamCoach: Proactive Sports Coaching via Continuous Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: In fitness and sports training, timely action quality assessment (AQA) is essential for learners to identify and correct technical errors during movement execution. However, most AQA methods assess completed performances, limiting their ability to provide timely feedback. Streaming methods alleviate this latency, but limited reasoning hinders their use of subtle movement cues and sport-specific knowledge. Moreover, their fragmented feedback focuses on one body part at a time, overlooking movement details of other body parts and transitions between action phases. To address these limitations, we propose StreamCoach, a streaming AQA framework under the OnCueCoaching paradigm that couples continuous chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning with proactive, evidence-gated coaching. Technique-Aware Reasoning tracks body-part movements and action-phase transitions against sport-specific criteria, while Holistic Coaching integrates accumulated evidence to deliver timely, comprehensive feedback on strengths and technical errors. To support training and benchmarking, we construct EE4D-Stream from 1,213 sports video sequences in Ego-Exo4D through LLM-assisted reannotation and manual review of selected claims, pairing dense CoT annotations with evidence-gated speech content. Building on this dataset, we train StreamCoach using Temporal-Semantic Alignment Reinforcement Learning to jointly optimize feedback timing and content. We benchmark 11 offline and streaming baselines on EE4D-Stream, including three proprietary models. StreamCoach achieves state-of-the-art results across intervention timing, action assessment, and coaching quality, surpassing both GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5.

papers.title: Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
papers.abstract: We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.

papers.title: Online outlier-resilient data-driven moving horizon estimation for linear discrete-time systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses data-driven state estimation for linear systems of which online output measurements may be corrupted by sparse outliers of arbitrary magnitude. Using only offline input-state-output data without explicitly identifying a system model, we propose an outlier-resilient data-driven moving horizon estimation scheme, termed OORD-MHE, based on Willems' fundamental lemma. The scheme employs a truncated-quadratic loss on the output residuals, parameterized by a truncation threshold, to mitigate the influence of online outliers. We establish sufficient conditions under which the resulting estimation error remains uniformly bounded. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed OORD-MHE scheme generates accurate state estimates in the presence of sparse online outliers.

papers.title: Quasiperiodicity breakdown and homoclinic bifurcations in the forced librations of a parametric oscillator
papers.abstract: Above its instability threshold, a parametrically excited oscillator settles into one of two phase states. The response of these states to a second, much slower modulation of the same stiffness is investigated. In the rotating frame, this modulation periodically varies the detuning and drives the phase librations. When the modulation is slow compared with the libration frequency, the phase states follow adiabatically. As the two frequencies become comparable, this approximation breaks down and the driven libration resonates with the intrinsic one. This nonadiabatic regime is examined for a Duffing oscillator with nonlinear damping. The averaged equations describe a periodically perturbed planar system with integrable unperturbed dynamics, whose homoclinic loop is derived in closed form. The phase states persist as invariant tori supporting quasiperiodic motion. Their stability and period-doubling bifurcations are captured by a damped Mathieu equation, in which the modulation contributes to both parametric stiffness and parametric damping. A Melnikov analysis yields explicit thresholds for separatrix splitting and the onset of homoclinic intersections, which are corroborated by numerical computations of the invariant manifolds. Numerically it is revealed that these intersections arise well before sustained chaotic motion develops. The fate of the parametric oscillation depends markedly on the resonance condition: modulation at the libration frequency destroys the invariant tori and quenches the oscillation, whereas modulation at twice the libration frequency leaves it intact.

papers.title: Studies of dual ions arriving time reconstruction in N$ν$DEx time projection chamber
papers.abstract: The N$ν$DEx experiment aims to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of \(^{82}\)Se with a high-pressure \(^{82}\)SeF\(_6\) negative-ion time projection chamber. In the assumed two-carrier model, the arrival-time separation of SeF\(_5^-\) and SeF\(_6^-\) can estimate the longitudinal coordinate without an external trigger. We compare FFT deconvolution and direct waveform fitting on simulated Topmetal-S charge-sensitive-amplifier waveforms. With the fixed amplifier response, direct fitting and FFT accepted 873 and 855 of 873 geometry-selected single depositions, respectively. On the 855 common events, the arrival-time separation RMSEs were 0.180 and 0.222 ms. Numerical depth calibration gave mean \(z\) residuals of 0.036 and 0.075 cm and RMSEs of 0.192 and 0.208 cm on 848 common events. With sampled CSA shaping, FFT accepted the same 855 waveforms and direct fitting accepted 866 of 873. On the four-way common sample of 855 events, the direct-fit separation RMSE was 0.180~ms with fixed shaping and 0.217~ms with sampled shaping. An accepted near-readout direct fit outside the FFT sample had a 184~ms separation error, giving an RMSE of 6.25~ms over all accepted sampled-response direct fits. With the fixed response, the full-track fit retained 1,185 of 1,810 observed pads in 100 selected Geant4 events. The median event-level depth RMSE was 0.184 cm. Subtracting each event's mean Monte Carlo residual gave a median event-centred RMS of 0.102 cm as a diagnostic of relative track shape. The absolute depth remains sensitive to the common event time. Validation with detector data is needed to assess the effects of diffusion, electronics noise, and inter-pad response.

papers.title: Weak oddness to resistance ratios in snarks
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. If $G$ is not 3-edge-colourable, we call it a \textit{snark}. The \textit{resistance} of $G$, denoted $r(G)$, is the minimum number of edges which can be removed from $G$ in order to render $G$ 3-edge-colourable. The \textit{oddness} of $G$, denoted $ω(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any 2-factor of $G$. The \textit{weak oddness} of $G$, denoted $ω'(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any even factor of $G$. In their comprehensive survey paper on measurements of uncolourability in cubic graphs, Fiol et al. conjectured the following two statements for a snark $G$: $ω(G) \leq 2r(G)$ and $ω'(G) \leq 2r(G)$ \cite{FiolMazzuoccoloSteffen2018}. Previously, we disproved the former by proving that the ratio of oddness to weak oddness, and hence the ratio of oddness to resistance, can in fact be arbitrarily large \cite{Allie2019}. In this paper, we prove a slightly stronger version of the latter: $ω'(G) < 2r(G)$. The proof centres around substructures in $G$, given a minimal colouring $f$, which we call \textit{meta-Kempe chains}.

papers.title: On the Design of a Slow Control Interlock System for the European GateMate FPGA
papers.abstract: Slow Control Systems (SCSs) are essential for the monitoring, configuration, and protection of distributed safety-critical systems in scientific, industrial, and medical applications. Although software-based SCS architectures offer flexibility and scalability, they suffer from software aging and non-deterministic latencies, which limit long-term reliability and timely reaction to critical errors, often requiring additional hardware interlock systems. This paper presents an FPGA-centric lightweight Slow Control Interlock System (SCIS) designed to achieve deterministic ultra-low-latency reaction times in long-running dependable systems. System parameters are acquired and fused at runtime in a Supervisory Monitor Unit (SMU), enabling real-time fault condition classification and prioritization through configurable priority rules and triggering kill-switch actions with microsecond-scale latency. The proposed SMU has been described in VHDL as vendor-agnostic architecture, and assessed on the 28-nm GateMate M1A1 FPGA, using the open-source OSS-CAD-Suite toolchain. Experimental results show that the SMU architecture utilizes only 37,6% of LUTs, 9,4% of FFs, and 35,9% of BRAM. Furthermore, this low resource utilization allow to achieve 40,48 ms reconfiguration time, using OSS-CAD-Suite including gmpack v1.13. This is a key metric for rejuvenation and consequently for enabling aging mitigation in critical applications. Offloading the Ethernet stack to the W5500 Ethernet module and integrating the Grafana dashboard provides a lightweight, deterministic SCIS. This demonstrates the feasibility of our FPGA-centric architecture as a solution to the problem of combining ultra-low-latency interlock capabilities with the scalability of software-based systems.

papers.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
papers.abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout prediction versus performing rollout prediction before downsampling. We observe that fine-scale dynamical details are often encoded in this gap. By commuting these two operations, the fine-scale details removed during downsampling can be captured. Furthermore, we employ a memory module to store these fine-scale features along the trajectory and retrieve them during rollout, generating spatially adaptive corrections that enhance long-horizon fidelity. Empirical results across five systems demonstrate that CoMNO improves prediction accuracy and long-horizon rollout stability.

papers.title: Periodic and quasiperiodic structures produced by microphase separation in one-component simple liquids with competing interactions
papers.abstract: Competing interactions can generate frustration which suppresses macroscopic-scale phase separation, superseding it with separation patterns on the microscopic scale. This phenomenon, referred to as microphase separation, produces thermodynamically stable mesoscopic-scale periodic patterns in systems of different physical nature. The studies of this effect follow two paradigms. First, in block copolymers, the macroscopic-scale separation of chemically distinct components is prevented by the covalent bonds between them. In the other, the microscopic-scale separation is produced in simple single-component liquids by the competition between a short-range attraction and a long-range repulsion (SALR) in the pair potential, the separation occurring between a dense phase and a gas. The interest in the simple liquid models with SALR interaction was inspired by the apparent universality of the modulated structures generated by competing interactions in different systems. Simple particle models are tractable by theory and thereby make it possible to discern the microscopic mechanisms of pattern formation; particle-based simulations give access to systems beyond the reach of experiments. In this Perspective we review the recent advances in the molecular-dynamics simulation of microphase separation in single-component simple liquids using SALR potentials. We show that these simulations reproduce the mesophases typical of block copolymers and liquid crystals, which demonstrates that the complexity of the constituent particles of real liquids is not a necessary condition for their formation, and that they produce novel periodic morphologies of both conceptual interest and technological relevance; we discuss how simulated mesophases can serve as templates for metamaterials whose properties are governed by topology.

papers.title: Commutator syzygies and pure resolutions over central polynomial rings with division-ring coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a division ring and let $A=D[x,y,z]$ with central indeterminates. For positive integers $p,q$ and $a,b\in D$, put $f=x^p+az^p$ and $g=y^q+bz^q$. We compute their left syzygy module and the minimal graded free resolution of $A/(Af+Ag)$. This quotient has projective dimension two if $ab=ba$ and three otherwise. In the latter case, it has finite length and total Betti numbers $(1,2,2,1)$, with a pure resolution of type $(0,d,3d,4d)$ when $p=q=d$. These tables do not occur over polynomial rings over fields. If $D$ is finite-dimensional over its center $K$, the Betti tables of modules of finite length over $K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and left modules of finite length over $D[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ generate the same rational cone for every $n\ge1$. In three variables, the semigroup over $K$ is properly contained in that over $D$ when $D$ is noncommutative.

papers.title: Semirings Induced by Semilattices
papers.abstract: We investigate semirings induced by join-semilattice (meet-semilattices) with a degenerate multiplication on all the subset that excludes the multiplicative unity. The way those semirings are defined enables a big impact of the semilattices we start with on the associated semirings: many of their order-theoretic properties reflect in algebraic properties of the induced semirings. This enabled constructing examples of semirings with desired properties as well as providing counterexamples to wrong claims in old and recent papers/preprints. In particular, we construct families of examples of semirings induced by non-modular join-semilattices for which the lattice of subtractive ideals is non-modular disproving a claim of Henriksen who introduced this important class of ideals of semirings.

papers.title: Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral
papers.abstract: The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $Λ(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i Φ(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. We prove that the tangent space of the mixture family is a Chebyshev system, which forces $2K$-point equioscillation at every interior minimiser and makes any such solution the unique global minimax, and we prove interior attainment for $K \le 11$. A certification algorithm audits a candidate mixture in multiple-precision arithmetic, using a proved bound on the number of extrema as its completeness test, and three search pipelines reach $K = 9, 10, 11$, the last with certified worst-case error $1.26 \times 10^{-11}$. A signed $K = 22$ mixture carries a relaxed certificate at $3.605 \times 10^{-15}$. In causal mediation with a binary outcome, the certified sum replaces a biased Taylor expansion and stochastic integration with one closed-form evaluation.

papers.title: Pando: Noise-Coupled Parallel Draft Trees for Efficient Edge Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) decoding emits one token per forward pass, reloading the full model each time, so LLM inference on edge devices is memory-bound while the compute units sit idle. Speculative decoding puts that idle compute to work by verifying several drafted tokens in a single pass. State-of-the-art parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark propose an entire block of draft tokens in one forward pass, which makes drafting compute-efficient. However, they are deployed with draft chains whose length is capped by the block size they are trained for, leaving most of the computational budget for verification unused. To tackle this problem, we propose Pando, which builds dynamic draft trees on top of a parallel drafter and thereby removes this cap. Pando employs noise-coupled pruning, which draws the target model's sampling noise before drafting and ranks candidate branches under that noise, so the tree retains the branches the target will actually sample. Noise coupling is lossless and requires no retraining or additional model pass, yet increases acceptance length by up to $8.4\%$ on Qwen3-8B. To optimize and evaluate Pando configurations across hardware, we normalize an operator-level roofline to AR decoding, reducing every platform to its ridge point. On a representative edge device, a 16-node Pando tree attains $5.3\times$ speedup and $4.2\times$ energy reduction over AR decoding: $25\%$ faster than DSpark's released chain, and $27\%$ faster and $72\%$ more energy-efficient than an EAGLE-3 tree. The best configurations remain memory-bound on every edge device we model, so added compute capacity does not reduce their latency.

papers.title: The 2026 iron meteorite fall near Zadzim (Poland) and atmospheric ablation of iron meteoroids
papers.abstract: Understanding the process of penetration of cosmic material through the Earth's atmosphere is important for linking the atmospheric and ground effects with the properties of original bodies. It has been shown previously that the main process affecting the fate of stony impactors is atmospheric fragmentation. Much less is known about iron impactors,mainly because the scarcity of data about actual iron meteorite falls. Here we present the trajectory, dynamics, light curve, spectrum, and orbit of a fireball which occurred on April 17, 2026, over Poland and was observed by the European Fireball Network and the Skytinel Network. Based on the fireball observations, single 2.9 kg iron meteorite was recovered in the municipality of Zadzim. Analysis of the fireball data revealed no fragmentation although the body suffered a relatively large dynamic pressure of 5.2 MPa. Fitting the light curve needed luminous efficiency 3 times larger than for stony meteoroids. The initial mass was about 19 kg, corresponding to an effective size of 17 cm. We fitted the light curves of 7 other fireballs produced by iron meteoroids with sizes of 2.5 - 13 cm. The ablation coefficient reached enormously high values of about 1 kg/MJ in small meteoroids causing the material to be exhausted and the fireball to end suddenly high in the atmosphere. In the present case, the value did not exceed 0.08 kg/MJ and relaxed to 0.023 kg/MJ towards the end, enabling part of the meteoroid to survive as meteorite. We conclude that the fate of iron meteoroids strongly depends on their size. The reason probably is the high thermal conductivity of iron which leads to complete overheating and easy melting of smaller meteoroids. The orbits of 44 iron fireballs are also provided.

papers.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
papers.abstract: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.

papers.title: Unjamming Deferrals: Supporting Students Through JAMN Bot, a Mobile RAG-Grounded Policy Assistant
papers.abstract: In some educational institutions, workflows such as the exam deferral process can be slow, inconvenient, and inconsistent, which creates the need to implement novel digital systems. This paper presents Schedulater, a mobile app for managing university exam deferrals. JAMN Bot is a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered chatbot integrated into Schedulater that provides context-aware support to help users understand the deferral process. The system features a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using Ollama (Llama 3.2 3B) for self-hosted inference which enables policy-grounded responses without sacrificing privacy. We evaluate the system using a 43-item benchmark spanning Exam Deferral, Privacy, Scheduling, Cross-Policy, and Adversarial & Out-of-Scope questions, and report inter-rater agreement among our human evaluators alongside retrieval hit-rate metrics. Subsequently, we utilize an LLM-as-a-judge approach with GPT-5.4, revealing slight-to-moderate alignment with our raters that improves with answer quality, and check the ranking against a panel including Gemini 3.5 Flash and Qwen3.5 397B. The results of our study display trade-offs between open-weight and frontier models, as well as LLM-human evaluation alignment with answer quality. Schedulater demonstrates the feasibility of integrating lightweight LLMs into university administrative workflows with structured retrieval.

papers.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
papers.abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). The 1T-derived structures remain metallic and magnetic throughout, with $U$ acting mainly as a spectral renormalization. The 1H phase behaves differently, passing from a non-magnetic semiconductor through an antiferromagnetic semiconducting regime before metallizing, so that the gap closes as $U$ increases while the local Cr moment grows monotonically. Biaxial tensile strain at fixed $U$ induces a similar sequence of transitions. Along both tuning pathways, the two inequivalent nearest-neighbor Cr--Cr exchange channels progressively separate and cross, with the parallel-spin channel becoming dominant, accompanied by a breathing-type bond disproportionation. Independent calculations with a localized-orbital implementation reproduce the overall evolution but yield shifted critical values of $U$ and of strain, demonstrating the robustness of the phase diagram while highlighting the implementation dependence of the transition thresholds.

papers.title: Mayfly: Lifecycle-Aware High-Bandwidth Flash for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets an LLM improve its agent system by proposing and evaluating candidate variants across tasks. A generation's sessions grow their KV caches together and release them as they finish, creating a burst followed by a decline. At high concurrency, even the KV of sessions ready to run exceeds the GPU's HBM. Offloading that KV to host DRAM or SSDs adds capacity but leaves ready sessions waiting for HBM space before execution. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) can serve the overflow in place, but excessive reads lengthen decode steps and repeated writes consume flash endurance. Our key insight is that where ready KV is read should follow the burst and its decline: from HBF in place while the burst overflows HBM, as much as each step's bandwidth allows, and from HBM again as the decline frees it. A switch between ready and parked decides only whether a block is read, so its flash copy stays valid, and a session's end, which the orchestrator announces, decides when its private KV dies. We present Mayfly, lifecycle-guided HBF management for RSI. Mayfly bounds per-step HBF reads during overflow and returns KV to HBM as sessions finish and free space. It retains a valid backing copy of each block evicted from HBM to avoid rewrites across state transitions, and forwards session-end signals to the controller to avoid copying dead KV during garbage collection. Experimental results show that, at 128 sessions per generation on four added HBF sites, Mayfly finishes 34% sooner than parking the same KV on HBF and 23% sooner than reading it from HBF whenever HBM is full; its gain over parking grows with concurrency, to 55% at 256 sessions on eight sites. Keeping one flash copy per block and trimming at announced session ends avoid write amplification.

papers.title: Linear convergence of evolution strategies to local minima by coupling with quadratic models
papers.abstract: Among derivative-free optimization methods, evolution strategies have emerged as competitive algorithms for multimodal, noisy or ill-conditioned problems in small and moderate dimensions. Theoretical guarantees have long been scarce, but a series of recent works established their convergence on certain classes of objective functions. A successful approach normalizes the states of the algorithm into a Markov chain and proves that this chain converges to a stationary distribution. It has yielded the linear convergence of several evolution strategies, including the state-of-the-art CMA-ES. Yet this approach requires the objective function to be scaling-invariant, hence unimodal, since otherwise the normalized process is not a Markov chain. We propose a methodology to prove linear convergence on a much larger class of functions, including smooth multimodal functions. Started close enough to a local minimum with a nondegenerate Hessian and with a small enough step size, the ($μ$/$μ$w, $λ$)-ES with stepsize adaptation converges linearly to this minimum with high probability, at the rate of its quadratic model, and the probability of failure vanishes when the initial step size and the initial distance to the minimum tend to zero. The proof views the normalized process as an adaptive chain and couples it, with high probability, with the Markov chain associated with the quadratic model.

papers.title: The Commutant of the Adjoint Center Need Not Be the Center of the Dual
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach lattice with ideal center $Z(X)$, and let $Z^*(X)=\{S^*:S\in Z(X)\}$ be the set of adjoints of central operators, acting on the dual $X^*$. The center $Z(X^*)$ of the dual is always contained in the commutant $(Z^*(X))^{\mathrm{com}}$ of $Z^*(X)$, and equality is known when $X$ has a topological order unit. It has been asserted that equality holds whenever $X$ has a topologically full center; the published proof of this assertion is incorrect, and the question has been recorded as open. We show that the assertion is false. For the Marcinkiewicz sequence space $m_ψ$, $ψ(t)=\log(1+t)$ (the sequence space underlying the Dixmier--Macaev ideal), which is Dedekind complete and therefore has a topologically full center, there is a bounded operator on the dual that commutes with every adjoint of a central operator but is not itself central; it maps one Dixmier trace onto another one disjoint from it. The construction rests on a general sufficient condition, proved with an invariant mean taking values in a Dedekind complete space $C(K)$ and the injectivity of $C(K)$. We also collect positive results and a norm-density criterion for equality. For every Orlicz space $L_Φ$ we show that every operator in $(Z^*(L_Φ))^{\mathrm{com}}$ is lower-triangular with respect to the decomposition of the dual into its order continuous and singular bands, with central diagonal entries, and, by a splitting lemma based on Young's inequality, that the off-diagonal entry vanishes. Hence equality holds for all Orlicz spaces and their duals, without any $Δ_2$-condition.

papers.title: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC
papers.abstract: Model-agnostic searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider utilise unsupervised anomaly detection, where quantum and neuromorphic detectors represent potential approaches. We develop the first fully spiking variational autoencoder, a quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on the quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron. In this work we recast the neuron from a measurement-based circuit to a differentiable computational unit. This neuron is benchmarked against other classical, spiking, and quantum models on an LHC di-jet latent space. We show that under noise perturbations the QLIF network retains $0.95$ of its clean accuracy, while accuracy retention for twelve classical models falls to $0.74$-$0.85$. The QLIF anomaly scores respond $3.5$-fold less to the noise perturbation than any of the control model's scores. We compare against a periodic classical control that reproduces the QLIF effect, isolating it to the $\sin^2$ membrane map. This membrane map is a native regulariser that decouples robustness from model capacity supplied by the qubit state space. We demonstrate this through several benchmarks and ablation studies to characterise the performance landscape of the quantum-neuromorphic model space.

papers.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
papers.abstract: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data. However, most methods still require wearable motion trackers and leave important hand-object interaction cues implicit. Many also mix in real-robot teleoperation data for VLA post-training. These dependencies limit scalable data collection, while implicit interaction cues make precise contact harder to learn. To overcome these limitations, we propose EgoLoAF, the first paradigm to derive all training data for humanoid loco-manipulation directly from egocentric demonstrations without wearable motion trackers. We post-train the VLA on the converted data alone, without real-robot teleoperation demonstrations, and use explicit hand-object interaction cues to guide action generation. Specifically, to obtain humanoid action targets, we estimate torso motion from recorded camera poses and reconstruct both hand trajectories from video. From the same recording, we use each hand's current pose relative to the object to represent hand-object affordances. During post-training, we inject these affordances into the action expert through cross-attention while keeping the vision-language backbone frozen. Additionally, we release 128,400 egocentric demonstration episodes spanning 1,000 hours and 1,284 tasks, together with converted humanoid action trajectories and rendered robot-view observations. Across four real-world tasks, EgoLoAF nearly achieves teleoperation performance (73.1 vs. 74.4 in mean Task Progress Score), while achieving a mean 4.03 times improvement in data-collection efficiency.

papers.title: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization
papers.abstract: Rydberg blockade can exclude the configuration that minimizes a binary objective. We expand its finite penalties into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs. The full ensemble preserves the ground energy, and the interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings. In simulations of two coupled squares, reversing a target coupling leaves the single-site energy slopes at uniform occupation unchanged, yet a collective mode of the residual interactions switches the favored diagonals from aligned to opposed. On 32 held-out twelve-site targets, the simulated probability of recovering a ground state in 128 shots averages 69.82\% with residual detunings and 24.31\% with a tuned uniform pulse. By scoring the pooled samples under the original objective, we can use these native layouts to search for ground states of a Hamiltonian that none implements alone.

papers.title: Energy and Performance Characterization of UxNBs: Toward AI-Driven Non-Terrestrial Open RAN Control
papers.abstract: UAV-mounted base stations (UxNBs) can provide ondemand 5G coverage, but their limited onboard energy makes power consumption the main operational constraint. AI-driven Open RAN controllers are a promising solution, yet they are trained almost exclusively on analytical models and simulations, since no public dataset captures the real energy behavior of a flying 5G base station (BS). As a first step toward closing this gap, we present a UAV testbed hosting a 5G picocell that supports a 20 MHz carrier and up to 100 Mbps throughput. The testbed measures BS system metrics, including power consumption, CPU load, and temperature, alongside UAV flight telemetry and detailed per-layer vRAN processing metrics. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that jointly exposes the energy and RAN behavior of a flying 5G BS, providing the real measurements needed to train and validate energy-aware AI controllers.

papers.title: Seldon TFM family: Seldon-Mini, Seldon and Seldon+
papers.abstract: We introduce Seldon, a family of tabular foundation models. Our classifier Seldon+ ranks first among 15 models on TabBench, our benchmark of 124 classification datasets, and on its variant with missing values. In our own runs of public benchmarks, it also ranks first on BeyondArena IID classification and TabBench-Bio, and second on TabArena classification. The open-weight models Seldon-Mini (27M parameters) and Seldon (213M parameters) both lie on the TabArena Pareto front of Elo against inference time: no entry is both more accurate and faster. On TabArena, Seldon ranks fourth and Seldon-Mini seventh among 109 leaderboard entries, and on the IID track of BeyondArena, Seldon ranks second among 42 entries. Seldon-Mini and Seldon handle both classification and regression, use an architecture similar to those of Kumo-Tabular, TabFM and TabPFN-3.5, and are trained on synthetic tables only.

papers.title: RoboDemo: Reconciling Demonstration Intent and Execution Progress for Long-Horizon Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires more than predicting the next action from the current observation. The policy must maintain a global procedural prior that specifies the expected progress of each subtask stage, while also tracking the realized progress produced by its interactions. To this end, we propose RoboDemo, a demonstration-augmented manipulation framework built on Dual-Cascaded Test-Time-Training. RoboDemo accepts either a task-relevant human demonstration video or a semantically compatible robot video retrieved from simulation corpus as reference, allowing us to evaluate its applicability with and without paired human demonstrations. Task semantics and physical motion information from the reference video are then transferred into persistent demonstration-intent memory. During deployment, we causally compress online observations, robot states, and executed actions into interaction-progress memory. To keep reference intent stable while interaction progress continually evolves, reference and execution video tokens independently update their respective fast-weight states. The action expert performs cascaded memory reads, first obtaining reference guidance and then refining it using realized progress, allowing the policy to adapt to execution deviations without overwriting the stored intent. RoboDemo achieves 90.7% success on Imitator Game and 73.3% success across three real-world household tasks. Real-world videos, code and hf-weights are available in our project website.

papers.title: TimeTravelContainer: A Live Forking Sandbox for Stateful Agent Exploration
papers.abstract: LLM agents that drive stateful tools (e.g., interactive shells, design environments, simulation engines) frequently need to clone, backtrack, and parallelize live sessions to support exploration. However, cloning a live session today requires serializing the tool's in-memory state to disk or relaunching from scratch, both prohibitively slow for interactive exploration. Existing agent sandboxes based on microVMs or kernel patches either serialize full guest memory to storage or require privileged deployment, limiting use on shared compute farms, personal computers, and other restricted environments. We present TimeTravelContainer (TTC), a rootless container runtime that live-forks an entire running container, including processes, memory, filesystem, and network, with copy-on-write (CoW) semantics. Because the bulk of a tool session's memory is typically read-only after the fork point, clones share it automatically and only diverged pages consume additional memory. TTC requires no kernel modifications, hardware virtualization, or root privileges, and runs on all major platforms including Linux, macOS (Apple Silicon), and Windows (WSL 2), making it deployable as a portable foundation for agent harnesses. We evaluate TTC on two agentic electronic design automation (EDA) flows as representative stateful-tool workloads: MAGE (Innovus) and EvoDRC (KLayout). TTC achieves 84.1$\times$ environment cloning speedup, 31--72% memory reduction, and 1.7--9.4$\times$ end-to-end speedup, demonstrating that live forking removes a scaling barrier for agent-driven exploration of stateful tool environments.

papers.title: Symmetry-dependent field-induced elastic renormalization in the quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy NiCoCr$_{0.8}$
papers.abstract: We investigate the elastic response of cubic NiCoCr$_{0.8}$, a quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy, by high-precision ultrasound velocity measurements. At zero magnetic field, the three symmetrically independent elastic moduli $C_{11}$, $(C_{11}-C_{12})/2=C_t$, and $C_{44}$ monotonically harden upon cooling without pronounced elastic softening or anomalies. In magnetic fields applied along [110], however, a minute but systematic elastic renormalization of the order of $10^{-5}$ is resolved at low temperatures. The tetragonal $E_g$ mode $C_t$ softens with increasing field, whereas the derived bulk $A_{1g}$ mode $C_B$ hardens, revealing an opposite field response between the two strain-symmetry channels. Comparison with the previously reported quantum-critical-Fermi-liquid crossover scale shows that the field-induced elastic renormalization develops already in the quantum-critical regime and evolves continuously across the crossover region, without a sharp elastic anomaly or threshold behavior. These results demonstrate that symmetry-resolved ultrasound provides a sensitive probe of subtle strain-dependent changes in the electronic and magnetic free energy of a chemically disordered itinerant quantum-critical metal.

papers.title: Rotationally symmetric fractional minimal surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary.

papers.title: CaveBench: Benchmarking Abductive Physical Reasoning from Internal Observations
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are advancing in physical reasoning, but whether they can understand external physical drivers from internal observations remains an open question. Existing benchmarks have not specifically targeted this setting. To this end, we introduce CaveBench, a benchmark for abductive physical reasoning from internal observations. Models receive apparatus descriptions and internal images while the external controls remain hidden, and must infer the operations responsible for the observed responses. CaveBench spans 20 apparatus scenes in five physical domains and contains 10,200 simulated episodes, split into 9,000 training, 1,000 validation, and 200 test episodes. Questions span one to six events and require the complete control set at every event, testing whether an explanation accounts for the entire process. Synchronized observations and control records provide the inputs and reference answers. Evaluating 27 VLM configurations yields six-event exact-match accuracies of 68.0% for the strongest closed-source model and 12.5% for the strongest open-weight model. Seven adaptation baselines show that single-event gains need not improve complete sequences. Error analysis identifies failures in visual identification, physical inference, evidence integration, and action composition, specifying where current models struggle to connect internal phenomena with their external causes.

papers.title: Sulfur chemistry in temperate N$_2$-dominated exoplanetary atmospheres investigated through experimental simulations: Volatile characterization
papers.abstract: Aims. This study addresses through an experimental approach an understudied aspect of sulfur atmospheric chemistry which is the coupled and complex reactivity existing between sulfur, carbon, and nitrogen elements. Experimental simulations have been used to better characterize the volatile products resulting from the coupling between these three elements and discuss the potential observability of such species. Sulfur chemistry appears as a source of diversified signatures which need to be characterized for the current and the future exploration of exoplanetary atmospheres. Methods. SO$_2$ and H$_2$S reactivity was explored experimentally in plasma discharges using mixtures of either pure N$_2$ or composed of N$_2$ and CH$_4$. The volatile species produced in such conditions were analyzed and quantified by in situ mass spectrometry. Results. SO$_2$ reactivity in the presence of N$_2$ alone or combined with methane led to the detection of six sulfur species: H$_2$S, NHSO, S$_2$O, CS$_2$, OCS, and CH$_3$SH. Under the same conditions, the reactivity of H$_2$S resulted in the observation of CS$_2$, CS, and CH$_3$SH. The detection of these species highlights the need to establish a consistent photochemical network describing this sulfur chemistry. Furthermore, the study addresses the detectability of these sulfur compounds via transit spectroscopy. Among them, OCS and CS$_2$, exhibit several detectable bands in the mid-infrared, and constitute promising targets to probe sulfur active chemistry with space- telescopes. In contrast, the detection of the other sulfur volatiles observed appears more challenging at low spectral resolution.

papers.title: On the bounds of path-unique subgraph of De Bruijn graph
papers.abstract: The De Bruijn graph is a directed graph G(n, m) such that V = (Zn)m and there is an edge from A to B iff A deletes the first coordinate equals to B deletes the last coordinate. Based on the background of achieving DNA labeling with minimum labels, we consider the De Brujin graph and its path-unique subgraph with maximum edges. Hofmeister gave an estimation of the lower bound and upper bound of the biggest number of the ratio of the edges we can keep in a path-unique subgraph, given the upper bound and lower bound and proved that the limit goes to 1 when n tends to infinity, and a lower bound m+1 2m when m tends to infinity. In this article, we will give some better construction of path-unique subgraph then give a better estimation in each condition, and show that when n tends to infinity the graph is almost (m + 1)-partite

papers.title: Minkowski problems for $(s,q)$-chord measures
papers.abstract: Motivated by the work of Lutwak--Xi--Yang--Zhang on the chord measures, we introduce the $(s,q)$-chord measures arising from variations of a new family of geometric invariants, called the $(s,q)$-chord integrals. When $s=1$, the $(s,q)$-chord measures recover the chord measures. We study the corresponding Minkowski problems for the \((s,q)\)-chord measure.

papers.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
papers.abstract: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted guidance in ascending order of the sum of its priority and trigger-strength ranks, which can surface high-risk guidance with weaker triggers. VerClin outperforms direct generation and Top-5 RAG on HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Professional. On the LLMEval-Med subset, it outperforms direct generation and ties Top-5 RAG. Component analyses further examine semantic closure, example-guided refinement, specialty screening, and constraint-conditioned delivery.

papers.title: SkillCore: Internalizing Generalizable Skills via Scaffolding-Removed Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Runtime skills can improve agents' problem-solving capabilities by providing procedural guidance for tasks such as code review and debugging. However, these benefits reach only a minority of users, as most do not proactively invoke skills in practice. We argue that such generalizable procedures should become part of the model's capabilities rather than remain optional external add-ons, making them directly available without explicit skill loading. To this end, we present SkillCore, a data pipeline and supervised fine-tuning recipe for internalizing generalizable skills. We transform real agent trajectories by removing skill-loading scaffolding while preserving the task context and subsequent agent actions, thereby supervising direct execution without external skill content. To preserve access to task-specific skills that provide genuinely external information, we mix these scaffold-removed trajectories with a small proportion of skill-native trajectories that preserve supervision for skill invocation. On a held-out skill-free evaluation, SkillCore improves task completion quality over the base Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-72B models by 54.4% and 24.8%, respectively, while preserving task-specific skill invocation on a separate probe and general coding performance on SWE-bench Verified.

papers.title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $π_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

papers.title: A sharp polygonal Finsler-Hadwiger inequality
papers.abstract: For every simple $n$-gon of area $A$ with side lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, we prove \[ \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \ge 4\tan\fracπ{n}\,A +c_n\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2, \qquad c_n=1-\frac{\tan(π/n)}{\tan(π/(n-1))}, \] with the convention $c_3=1$, so that the case $n=3$ is exactly the Finsler-Hadwiger inequality. The coefficient $c_n$ cannot be improved, and equality holds only for regular polygons. The extremal configurations are far from the regular $n$-gon: the constant is approached by cyclic polygons in which one side shrinks to zero while the others become the sides of a regular $(n-1)$-gon (a doubled segment when $n=3$). The proof combines the classical fact that cyclic polygons maximize area for given side lengths with a two variable minimization using the half central angles. We also compute the larger optimal coefficient for nearly regular polygons, and show that the best constant in the joint stability estimate for side lengths and vertex radii grows like $n^2$.

papers.title: Magnetic vector fields with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We construct unit-length, divergence-free vector fields tangent to the boundary on arbitrary smoothly bounded domains in $\mathbb R^3$. These vector fields are continuously differentiable except for a finite number of points on the boundary. Our approach identifies a form of h-principle and a close analogy with Nash's construction of smooth isometric embeddings.

papers.title: Can You Find the Edit When Nothing Looks Wrong? A Paired Benchmark for Text-Driven Image Manipulation Localization Beyond Semantic Abnormality
papers.abstract: Instruction-driven image editing can alter a photograph while keeping the result coherent with the scene. Existing benchmarks lack matched plausible and anomalous edits of the same target, making it difficult to measure how localization performance changes with semantic plausibility. We construct a paired benchmark by generating semantically plausible and anomalous replacements of the same target in each source photograph. Both edits use the same editor, language, and generation settings. We estimate a separate mask for each output and retain pairs with sufficient mask overlap, enabling direct comparison of localization performance under the two semantic conditions. The release contains 47,747 bilingual triplets from 6,500 photographs, spanning four editors, three source domains, and six intended violation types. Across nine public localizers, editor-averaged IoU is lower on plausible edits in 26 of 27 model-dataset comparisons. This gap persists under pixel-change controls and region-size analyses. These findings reveal a semantic-plausibility shortcut: localization often weakens when an edited result looks ordinary. The benchmark provides a controlled setting for measuring this gap and developing localizers that remain effective on plausible edits.

papers.title: Motion Chain of Thought: Disentangling Motion Semantics from Visual Appearance for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding action generation. However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions. This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening the predictive capability of world evolution modeling for action generation. We propose PILOT (Physical Inference for Latent Optimized Trajectories), whose core Representational Deduction (RD) bridges this gap by integrating motion chain-of-thought (CoT) guidance as a native model capability. Specifically, RD aims to encourage the action branch to explicitly model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as CoT in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectory. Experiments demonstrate that RD not only improves the success rate and generalization ability of WAMs in complex robotic manipulation tasks but also enhances the model's physical interpretability by decoupling high-level motion semantics from low-level trajectory details. Furthermore, the abundant state transition supervision signals introduced by RD effectively alleviate the sparse supervision in action generation, supporting data-efficient real-robot adaptation with reduced demonstration sets.

papers.title: The Insertion-Deletion Distance of Linear Codes under Random Coordinate Permutations
papers.abstract: We study the maximum insertion-deletion (insdel) distance attainable by permuting the coordinates of a fixed $[n,k]_q$ linear code. Exploiting the connection between common subsequences of codewords and noncrossing matchings in the related bipartite graphs, we establish probabilistic lower bounds under random coordinate permutations over large alphabets. In particular, if the maximum symbol multiplicity among nonconstant codewords is $O(n/q)$, a uniformly random coordinate permutation yields insdel distance at least $2n-O(n/\sqrt q)$ with high probability for sufficiently large $q$. Furthermore, for projective linear codes satisfying the same symbol multiplicity condition, we show that the maximum attainable insdel distance is $2n-Θ(n/\sqrt q)$. As an application, for $[n,k]_q$ MDS codes containing the all-one vector, random coordinate permutations yield insdel distance at least $2n-O(\sqrt{kn})$ with high probability whenever $(k-1)(\log q)^2=o(n)$. In particular, for full-length Reed--Solomon (RS) codes, we obtain the lower bound $2q-O(\sqrt{kq})$ with high probability for $k=o(q/(\log q)^2)$, substantially improving previously known lower bounds while allowing a wider range of dimensions. Finally, we give explicit constructions of full-length RS codes over square fields, attaining the order-optimal insdel distance $2q-Θ(\sqrt q)$.

papers.title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
papers.abstract: While quantum protocols for oblivious transfer can be built from weaker assumptions than classical ones, the current protocols remain highly impractical due to stringent security bounds that demand a large amount of quantum communication. In this work, we propose an enhancement to quantum oblivious transfer protocols by leveraging zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). At a high level, we modify the protocol such that the receiver proves that they are following honestly some crucial steps of the protocols, without revealing extra information to the sender. This yields a tighter security bound against a malicious receiver. For practical scenarios with a fixed security target, this approach reduces the amount of required quantum communication by one to two orders of magnitude, depending on the specific parameters. Furthermore, the benefits of our approach become particularly pronounced at higher qubit error rates, and our proposal even extends the maximum tolerable error rate of the quantum channel from approximately 3.5% to about 9%. The ZKP, however, introduces a substantial computational overhead, estimated to significantly exceed the acquisition time of the protocol, which is usually the primary bottleneck. To address this limitation, we also introduce a variant that serves as a tunable trade-off between the protocol with and without our modification. This enables precise adjustment of the computational overhead while still retaining significant, albeit moderately reduced, efficiency gains.

papers.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments with diverse start poses, yielding a wide and well-defined boundary that can be communicated to the agent through a simple handoff protocol. Second, Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement retrains the policy on curated successful system rollouts, extending the boundary toward earlier stages of each task and allowing the agent to hand over sooner with fewer language-model calls. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo, our system outperforms the strongest baseline by over 26 percentage points, reaching 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, while further reducing its API cost and execution time by 41.3% and 37.5%, respectively. These results suggest that the key to robust agent-policy orchestration lies not only in improving either component individually, but also in explicitly shaping the boundary between them.

papers.title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. (Quantum Theory from First Principles, 2017). Both of them refer to compound systems, the theory of which is rather directly assumed to be given by the tensor product structure. This structure, though well understood, should, however, be based on a more careful study of formal composition rules describing how local effects can be embedded into the compound effect space and how to reduce joint states onto subsystems. In that we follow the earlier work of T. Matolcsi, (Acta Sci. Math., 1975), and D. Aerts and I. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. We also establish axioms of local discrimination stating that compound states can be told apart by local measurements the notion of which we also formally define. The purification axioms first introduced as axioms of quantum mechanics by D'Ariano et al. are also rewritten in a weaker form which we believe could be fruitful for future axiomatizations. These reformulations bring us closer to proper tensor product structures for joint state and effect spaces, so that the embedding map for states factors through the projective tensor product of the local state spaces and the embedding map for effects factors through the injective tensor product of the local effect spaces. We also discuss the case of multipartite composition axioms and associativity properties required in these settings.

papers.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
papers.abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic.
