Retrieval-based curation selects the candidates that are most similar to the target demonstrations. Since it does not use the policy, any candidate that looks similar receives a high score. Performance-aware curation therefore estimates the effect of each candidate on the policy. However, this requires training on the candidates and takes a long time. We propose a third branch, policy-intrinsic curation, which uses the policy and still takes little time. It estimates this effect with forward passes of the pretrained policy and needs no training. We instantiate this branch with PICKER (Policy-Intrinsic Curation from Known Errors). It selects the candidates on which the policy makes errors that agree with those on the target demonstrations. PICKER reaches success rates comparable to those of performance-aware curation and takes about as long as retrieval-based curation. Its selection is also stable across seeds.

papers.title: Spin-adapted state preparation for quantum chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum phase estimation for strongly-correlated molecules requires an initial state of high overlap with the true ground state, and preparing one is a significant fault-tolerant cost. Matrix product states (MPS) produced by the density matrix renormalisation group (DMRG) are a leading choice, yet existing circuits treat their tensors as dense or do not use the full symmetries present in molecular electronic Hamiltonians. In quantum chemistry, DMRG also exploits total spin, a non-abelian symmetry, storing one amplitude per spin multiplet instead of one per state. We show that the reduced tensors of such a spin-adapted MPS, labelled by the steps of the unitary group approach, form an abelian-symmetric MPS, which existing block-sparse preparation protocols can load at a cost set by the multiplet count. One state-independent rotation per site, determined by a Clebsch-Gordan coefficient, then returns the state to the occupation basis. We provide resource estimates for our circuits on singlet ground states of active space models of iron-sulphur clusters, finding improvements in Toffoli count up to $135\times$ compared to dense methods and $4.9\times$ compared to block-sparse methods applied to the same states, with up to $3.7\times$ fewer ancilla qubits required.

papers.title: One Size Doesn't Fit All: Input Adaptive Class Activation Mapping for Improved Visual Explanations
papers.abstract: Despite their widespread use in tasks such as image classification, object detection and semantic segmentation, the limited interpretability of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) can undermine trust and hinder adoption in safety-critical applications. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods seek to address this by providing human-understandable explanations for model predictions. Class Activation Maps (CAM) constitute one such widely used XAI technique for visualizing discriminative regions. However, existing CAM methods may exhibit limitations in channel weighting, localization, and adaptability across network architectures potentially resulting in noisy or imprecise explanations. To address these issues, we propose ADAPT-CAM, a gradient-based, parameter-adaptive CAM framework. The method combines first-order gradient energy with activation-weighted second-order curvature to derive channel contributions. It further incorporates adaptive local contrast normalization and knee-guided soft channel selection to refine the resulting explanations. Importantly, key parameters are estimated independently for each input, allowing the framework to adapt to variations in feature representations across network architectures. We validate ADAPT-CAM on ImageNet and Oxford 102 Flowers across CNN and ViT architectures. Quantitative results demonstrate competitive or superior performance against established CAM methods across multiple evaluation metrics. In parallel, qualitative comparisons illustrate its ability to highlight discriminative image regions. Further parameter analysis and ablation experiments examine the behaviour and contributions of the individual adaptive components. These findings demonstrate the applicability of ADAPT-CAM across different architectures and datasets.

papers.title: Differential Proteomics to Symbolic Rules: An Audit of SHAP Guidance in Lung Adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: We tested whether SHAP improves protein-based Horn rules for distinguishing lung adenocarcinoma from adjacent-normal tissue. CPTAC supplied 213 samples (111 tumour, 102 adjacent-normal) from 111 patients, including 102 matched pairs. Per-protein effects and tests used the same complete pairs with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Sparse logistic regression used five stratified patient-grouped outer folds, with preprocessing and tuning confined to training data and feature selection repeated within inner folds. A separate five-fold patient-grouped evaluation of inductive logic programming used training-derived evidence and discretisation. Of 9,518 proteins passing quality control, 378 differed in abundance (40 up, 338 down) at FDR below 0.05 and an absolute mean paired log-ratio difference of at least 1. Classifier ROC-AUC, average precision, accuracy and balanced accuracy were 0.9997, 0.9998, 0.9906 and 0.9906, respectively. On the original held-out rule splits, accuracy and F1 were 0.9765 and 0.9774, respectively. One clause appeared in two folds and the others appeared once. On common folds across all 111 patients, F1 was 0.9600 with SHAP, 0.9910 without SHAP and 0.9909 for L1 logistic regression. The inclusive SHAP cutoff retained all 100 ranked proteins per audited fold. Absolute logistic-regression coefficients reproduced the SHAP-guided candidate sets, clauses and held-out predictions in both the all-patient and paired-only analyses. A single-protein threshold reproduced full-rule predictions in the paired-only cohort. SHAP guidance did not improve held-out F1 on the common folds. Diagnostic utility, early detection, prognosis and generalisability beyond this cohort remain unestablished. Biomarker and clinical claims require independent validation, rule-stability testing under repeated resampling and further biological annotation.

papers.title: Packing Stern into L2: GPU-Accelerated Primal-Shortened ISD for High-Codimension Binary Goppa Key Recovery
papers.abstract: Primal-Shortened Information-Set Decoding (ISD) with quadratic polar lifting recently pushed TII McEliece Track-2 key recovery to $mt=126$ (TII-228, $2{,}463$ CPU core-hours), with over $99\%$ of runtime spent harvesting weight-$(2t+1)$ codewords. Porting MiniMax's Mode-6 Stern sampler directly to one block per SM leaves $1.0\text{-}1.5\text{ GB}$ of hash tables active and stalls on global memory. We pack $128$ syndrome bits into one $16$-byte ulonglong2 without left-triple indices (lossless for $mt \le 145$, and extended to $mt \le 192$ via truncated range pre-filtering), share $G \in \{4, 8\}$ cooperative tables inside GPU L2 cache, batch $64G$ random systematic reductions per launch, and widen the shortening prefix $n'$ to cut modeled GPU-hours by $34\%\text{-}47\%$. Across five Track-2 challenges ($mt = 108 \to 153$), every recovered private key passes both the official SageMath checker and a standalone pure-Python verifier. Eight Modal L40S GPUs solve TII-228 ($mt=126$) in $18.9\text{ min}$ ($2.15$ GPU-hours, $3.0\times$ faster in wall-clock than MiniMax's EPYC cluster). We further recover keys for the previously undocumented challenges TII-237 ($mt=135$, $22.1$ L4 GPU-hours), TII-235 ($mt=144$, $39.62$ L40S GPU-hours, $17.97\text{ s}$ lift), and TII-185 ($mt=153$, $140.4$ L40S + $\approx 60$ L4 GPU-hours, $39.01\text{ s}$ lift). These results do not demonstrate practical recovery against Classic McEliece parameters ($mt \ge 768$).

papers.title: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. Multi-session evaluation demonstrates that the constructed memory can be reused, while deployment on a real quadruped robot further shows the system's applicability. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav-1.5/

papers.title: Trajectory Visibility at First Sight
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a simple polygon with $n$ vertices, and let two moving entities $q(t)$ and $r(t)$ travel at constant (possibly distinct) speeds $v_q$ and $v_r$ along line-segment trajectories $τ_q$ and $τ_r$ inside $P$. We study the first-visibility time $ t^* = \min\bigl\{\,t \ge 0 \mid \overline{q(t)\,r(t)} \subseteq P\,\bigr\}, $ the earliest moment at which the segment joining $q(t)$ and $r(t)$ lies entirely within $P$. Prior work by Eades et al.~\cite{swat2020,eeades-phd} focused on the decision version of this question in a simple polygon. They gave a one-shot decision algorithm running in ${O}(n)$ time. For a stationary entity and a moving one, they gave a data structure with ${O}(n \log n)$ preprocessing time and ${O}(n)$ space that answers decision queries in ${O}(\log n)$ time. For two moving entities, after ${O}(n \log^5 n)$ preprocessing time, they built a data structure of size ${O}(n \log^5 n)$ with ${O}(n^{3/4}\log^3 n)$ query time. Variants for polygonal domains with holes or when entities cross the boundary of $P$ lie beyond our scope. In this work, we go beyond decision to compute $t^*$ exactly under three models for a simple polygon $P$. When both trajectories are fixed in advance, we preprocess $P$ in ${O}(n)$ time and space and answer each query $(v_q, v_r)$ in ${O}(\log n)$ time. If one trajectory $τ_r$ is fixed while $τ_q$ is given as a query, we build a structure in ${O}(n \log n)$ time and space that computes $t^*$ in ${O}(\log^2 n)$ time per query. When neither trajectory is known in advance, we develop a data structure with ${O}(n^{1+\varepsilon})$ expected preprocessing time and ${O}(n)$ space that achieves ${O}(n^{1/2}\,\text{polylog}(n))$ expected query time for any fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.

papers.title: Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
papers.abstract: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{ρ,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.

papers.title: Sánchez, Feijóo, or Abascal? Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X of the Leaders of the Three Main Parties of the 29N General Election in Spain
papers.abstract: Source cues are central to political communication, yet reception studies with large language model (LLM) personas as synthetic audiences have not tested whether personas respond to who speaks and not only to what is said. With Spain's general election of 29 November 2026 in mind, we run a speaker-attribution experiment using 1,075 anonymised X posts by the leaders of PSOE, PP and VOX on four topics (the economy and employment, household costs, immigration and corruption) and 791 distinct value-grounded, LLM-generated personas. Each post was assigned to 300 topic-selected persona profiles, 150 grounded in the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map and 150 in Moral Foundations Theory, under four conditions: no author, Sánchez, Feijóo or Abascal, yielding 322,470 complete persona-post quartets. Naming any leader lowered support for identical text, with the penalty for Abascal nearly twice as large as those for Sánchez and Feijóo. The penalty follows the persona's elicited left-right self-placement (ideological congruence): left personas spare Sánchez and right personas spare Feijóo, although ideology was never in the message-evaluation prompt. Corruption posts were penalised under every name, whereas on other topics the ideologically closest leader generally produced little or no penalty. The leader order matches public opinion in 48 CIS barometers (2022-2026) in all three groups and the sign of all twelve differences, but fits barometers before the model's 2024 knowledge cutoff better than recent ones. Our findings demonstrate that LLM personas evaluate political speakers through systematic, value-congruent priors: however, while they replicate human candidate rank-orders across survey barometers, this alignment is ordinal rather than quantitative, highlighting their utility for controlled source-effect experiments though not as substitutes for empirical public opinion surveys.

papers.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
papers.abstract: Let $φ_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $φ_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $φ_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alpöge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.

papers.title: Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
papers.abstract: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish. Using only Feynman diagrams, we verify this cancellation explicitly through third order. After continuation to negative coupling, the formal zero mode becomes nonnormalizable. A real instanton remains, but its one-instanton contribution to \(E_0\) vanishes. In particular, the leading shift in energy arises from a complex neutral bion. Taking an exact constrained family, we calculate its local median amplitude through two loops. The direct diagrammatic sum gives $c_{\rm 2L}^{\rm diag}=-0.750000(5)$, in excellent agreement with the exact-WKB value $-3/4$.

papers.title: SparQ4D: Learning to Act through Sparse 4D Queries
papers.abstract: Successful manipulation requires a policy to understand where things are and how they will move, yet action demonstrations leave this spatiotemporal structure implicit. While explicit 4D supervision has proven effective, reducing the cost of dense 4D prediction remains challenging. This paper introduces SparQ4D, a lightweight yet expressive decoder that efficiently injects holistic 4D scene understanding into policies and improves success rates. At its core is a query-based decoder attached to a pretrained policy, which casts many spatialtemporal tasks into one unified interface (e.g. depth, 2D/3D point motion, multi-view correspondence, and hand-eye relations). This design enables efficient training and inference without sacrificing expressivity: the policy learns rich 4D structure from a small number of sampled queries during training, while the decoder can be removed at inference with zero additional overhead. Across multiple backbones, simulated environments, and real-world settings, SparQ4D achieves state-of-the-art manipulation performance, outperforming competing methods while training up to $5\times$ faster. Probing analyses further reveal that this 4D structure is recoverable from the policy.

papers.title: PROPS: Can Visual Generators Keep the Current Look of a Prop?
papers.abstract: Many generation tasks draw the next image from a visual history, such as storyboards, illustrated stories and multi-turn editing. A new request often states what happens next without restating how earlier objects look. Instead of recovering an object's current look from the history, generators often redraw it from the request alone or bring back an outdated look, and the error can carry into later steps. We call this failure prop drift. Existing evaluations rarely isolate it, because similarity to the history rewards copying and a judge that sees a single history cannot tell a look recovered from that history from one the generator happens to prefer. We introduce PROPS, a benchmark of 2,257 pairs of twin histories that end on the same request but show one prop in two different looks. A pair passes only if the generator draws the matching look on each side and carries out the request, so a look preferred by the generator or the judge passes at most one side. All 34 open and closed systems we test show prop drift, and even systems that carry out the requested action on most sides often lose the current look of the prop. Swapping the planners and editors of agents further shows that both history understanding and image generation limit agent performance. We also build PROPS-Train, 80,250 training chains in four tracks whose targets recover an earlier state or carry scripted changes forward, and fine-tuning on it clearly improves all four tested models. Both datasets will be publicly released.

papers.title: Rotational Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
papers.abstract: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

papers.title: Social Interaction Breaks Replicate Independence in Controlled-Clone LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM evaluations and social simulations create many agents from one model and treat them as independent replicates, even after the agents interact. This assumption remains untested with matched controls. We introduce SocCogEval, a controlled-clone assay for Social Cognitive Transfer (SCT). Clones share the base model, system prompt, and decoding parameters and differ only in a private brief, and a factorial protocol separates the brief, 30 rounds of interaction, and initialization noise. On Qwen3-122B-FP8, interaction with the briefs held fixed raises off-topic BFI-10 response-profile drift by $\barΔ=+0.917$ and $+0.912$ in two topically disjoint scenarios (exact $p=0.0008$ and $0.0039$). The drift is larger than under the brief alone, persists under temperature-zero re-probing, and stays positive without typed memory extraction in exploratory tests. Matched solo generation reproduces part of it, and social interaction remains highest. Across five more model variants, every scenario-averaged interaction contrast is positive. Each interacting population is therefore one replicate, and treating its agents as independent requires paired no-interaction controls.

papers.title: S$2$SCORE: A Textless Unified Evaluation Metric for Speech-to-Speech Translation Systems
papers.abstract: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2$SCORE is trained using supervision derived from established evaluation models, enabling scalable learning without direct human annotations. Evaluated across five language pairs, S$2$SCORE shows strong agreement with human judgments, independent reference metrics, and the training supervision metrics, indicating robust generalization. The reference-free variant, S$2$SCORE-QE, consistently outperforms S$2$SCORE-REF and achieves stronger semantic adequacy prediction than BLASER~$2.0$.

papers.title: Seeing vs. Knowing: Counterfactual Supervision and Correction for 3D-Aware Object Editing
papers.abstract: Rotating, translating, or rescaling an object in a photograph requires revealing unseen surfaces, preserving visible appearance, and updating shadows and reflections. Reconstructed 3D assets, rendered at the target pose as a 3D state, provide explicit geometric guidance, but their imperfect textures may conflict with the photograph, while standard paired training does not explicitly teach the editor which source to trust. To address this, we propose counterfactual state supervision, which constructs controlled photo--state conflicts through hidden-surface repainting, hidden geometry with re-rendered shadows and reflections, and visible-surface texture replacement. This teaches the editor to follow the 3D state for unseen content while preserving photograph-visible appearance. However, learning this distinction does not ensure that it is maintained during sampling. We therefore introduce symmetric counterfactual correction, which uses state-side and photo-side twins, which share the photograph and the state respectively, to construct directed latent perturbations toward condition-inconsistent targets and train recovery toward the target specified by the current condition. Both strategies operate only during training, requiring no architectural changes or additional inference steps. Experiments on OBJect and SpatialEdit-Bench demonstrate strong spatial editing performance and content preservation, while controlled ablations show improved source selection and sustained responsiveness to conditioning during sampling.

papers.title: Collineations of particles as a tool to study nucleation and crystallization processes in liquids
papers.abstract: We suggest several methods that can be used for identification of crystal nuclei in the studies of the nucleation and crystallization processes in multicomponent systems and in situations when the forming crystalline phase is different from the FCC, HCP or BCC lattices. The approaches are based on consideration of collineations of particles. They allow finding nuclei and separating them from each other. We demonstrate the methods by considering two systems. For a single-component system, we perform a comparison between the results derived from the collineations and those obtained using the coarse-grained bond-orientational order parameters. Further, we illustrate the methods by considering the crystallization process in a Wahnström binary $BA_2$ system forming a rather complex crystal structure.

papers.title: NPUFHE: An Efficient CKKS Execution System for Ascend NPUs
papers.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation directly on encrypted data, but its substantial computational cost hinders adoption in privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Neural processing units (NPUs) already deployed in AI infrastructure provide a practical platform for FHE acceleration. However, after mapping the number theoretic transform (NTT) to matrix multiplications on Ascend NPUs, modular arithmetic and representation conversion on the Vector backend still incur substantial overhead at stage boundaries. Evaluation-key material of key switching also increases storage and data-transfer costs, and whole-limb task assignment causes tail load imbalance. We present NPUFHE, an end-to-end CKKS execution system optimized for Ascend NPUs. To reduce modular recovery and twiddle costs in NTT, we propose Boundary-Optimized NTT, which eliminates intra-axis modular recovery, compiles intra-axis twiddle factors into matrix constants, and introduces two-level folded modular recovery at axis endpoints. To alleviate evaluation-key storage and transfer pressure, we design Compact Shoup encoding, which halves the key representation through local coefficient recovery. Finally, we propose Cost-Aware Parallel Tiling to mitigate tail load imbalance caused by whole-limb task assignment. It uses a cost model to adaptively partition tail tasks and smooth stepwise latency increases. We integrate the above designs into OpenFHE. On one Ascend 910B4, full-packing CKKS bootstrapping with real evaluation keys takes 0.95 s, encrypted CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 inference with bootstrapping requires 9.87 s per image, and encrypted MNIST inference achieves an amortized latency of 19.81 ms per image. The peak NTT throughput of NPUFHE reaches up to $184.22\times$, $2.04\times$, and $4.46\times$ that of OpenFHE on CPU, TensorFHE, and CROSS, respectively.

papers.title: DuetFHE: Compiling Dual-Lane Nonlinear Circuits for Complex-Packed CKKS Inference
papers.abstract: Complex packing in CKKS stores two real streams in the real and imaginary lanes of each slot. Direct squaring couples the lanes, while squaring them separately requires two ciphertext-ciphertext multiplications (HMults). DuetFHE is a GPU compiler that uses a phase transformation to square both lanes independently with one HMult. It reuses dual-lane squares in polynomial activations and the modular-reduction stage of CKKS bootstrapping. The compiler further plans ciphertext scales and reuses conjugates to sustain the complex-packed representation across stages. On a single RTX 5090, DuetFHE accelerates four polynomial activations by $1.60$--$1.79\times$ over direct evaluation on two real ciphertexts. For two-image AESPA ResNet-20 inference, it maintains packed execution across convolutions, square activations, and bootstrapping, achieving a $1.97\times$ end-to-end speedup over the fastest tested EasyFHE batched baseline on both the RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000.

papers.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar Hölder domains
papers.abstract: Every nonzero real eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded simply connected planar Hölder domain has no interior critical point. The Hölder condition is quasihyperbolic; equivalently, a Riemann map has derivative in $L^{2p}$ for some $p>1$. This includes Lipschitz domains and polygons with reentrant corners. Multiple eigenvalues and non-Jordan boundaries are allowed. The proof uses boundary primitives, a uniform multiplier estimate, and approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace. When this eigenspace is two-dimensional, every real basis gives global coordinates onto a domain star-shaped about the origin. A stream function proves injectivity and yields a Poisson formula for the boundary angular derivative. The conformal boundary map has a Lipschitz inverse and a rectifiable Jordan image; its boundary angle is a circle diffeomorphism with nonvanishing Hölder-continuous derivative. The image can be nonconvex even when the source is smooth and strictly convex.

papers.title: Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness
papers.abstract: Under classical assumptions, performance of first-order methods has been studied quite comprehensively with the developed theoretical apparatus of modern optimization. The development of the Performance Estimation Problems (PEP) framework led to even deeper understanding and allowed computer-assisted derivation of exact worst-case guarantees. Unfortunately, PEP is not directly applicable for systems that involve SDP-incompatible constraints. This includes a wide range of non-standard assumptions, some of them are highly relevant for practice such as generalized smoothness. In this paper proposes an approach of utilizing template solutions to derive guarantees in settings that do not admit an equivalent SDP formulation of exact worst-case performance problem. The approach is showcased by studying the performance of the gradient descent method for convex functions that also satisfy $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness assumption. Despite the inherent conservatism of the approach, this paper improves and generalizes an existing convergence guarantee to showcase the approach.

papers.title: When Can a Rewiring Control Test LLM Weight Readers? C2 and an Eligibility Protocol
papers.abstract: Large language models can predict the outputs of small neural networks from raw weights, but success could reflect recognition of weight-space regularities (fingerprints) rather than computation, and function-preserving controls cannot tell these apart. We propose C2, a counterfactual that permutes the columns of a network's final linear readout: every other parameter, and the readout's singular values, norms and entry multiset, are unchanged, and the function can change in an exactly recomputable way; we verify that each evaluated permutation does. C2 separates fingerprinting from computation only under three conditions, which we state as an eligibility protocol: a strategy restricted to C2-invariant summaries must already predict the target; C2 must change a property specific to the rewiring; and the reader's identity must be attested. No natural setting we tested is eligible. On tiny MLPs a frontier reader route followed the rewired function on all 24 networks, but invariant baselines were near chance and its backend could not be attested. In two public CNN zoos the conditions traded off: weight statistics predicted CIFAR-10 accuracy in-distribution, but C2's effect on accuracy was not specific to the swap, while per-image targets were specific but not predictable from invariant summaries. On a constructed population where a planted fingerprint rule works, all conditions hold and C2 separates a rule-following reader from an executor. A self-hosted Qwen3.8-27B followed the rewired function rather than the shortcut, and showed no evidence of using the weights with thinking disabled. A registered replication on fresh networks confirmed both findings (tracking minus stuck 0.875, 95% interval [0.750, 1.000]), and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B also followed the rewiring (tracking minus stuck 0.729 [0.552, 0.885]). The transforms, audits and raw records are available from the authors.

papers.title: Interface Invariants of Rhombohedral Graphene with Layer-dependent Potentials and Couplings
papers.abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

papers.title: Exact stress-tensor fluctuations from conformal symmetry and black hole radiation
papers.abstract: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $α$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives the variance in closed form. The relative fluctuation scales as $1/c$, with $c$ the central charge. For the Schwarzschild black hole it is $22/5c$ for the Hawking flux at infinity, that of flat-space thermal radiation. At the horizon it is $-44α/3c$ for the outgoing flux and $(238+720α)/5c$ for the ingoing flux that drives the backreaction. Both reduce to $22/5c$ for $α=-3/10$, which corresponds to the Möbius-covariant prescription. For large $c$ these results support the semiclassical approximation.

papers.title: BO-COMM: Bidirectional Optical System for Simultaneous Localization and Communication in Swarm Robotics
papers.abstract: Swarm robotics experiments need to track where robots are, know what state each robot is in, and feed environmental information back to them. Reporting states over a shared radio channel can suffer from contention as the number of robots grows, while static fiducial markers provide pose but cannot report changing states. We present BO-COMM, a bidirectional optical system that observes pose and state through one camera and returns environmental cues through light. Each Colias IV robot, fitted with a CEU-PLUS extension unit, carries a ring of 12 LEDs: a five-bit marker encodes heading, and the remaining seven bits display one of 52 state codes. An overhead camera locates robot centers by ring-based voting and decodes position, heading and state for all visible robots from a single frame. In the downstream direction, a projector renders spatial cues such as virtual pheromone fields, and an infrared channel delivers addressed commands. At 2048x1280 resolution, image-processing time increases only modestly from 2 to 30 robots. Path-following, color-reporting and multi-pheromone experiments show the system closing the loop between optical state reports and projected environmental feedback in a 2.50 x 1.56 m arena.

papers.title: LITMUS - Literature Informed Testbed for Mapping Usecases and Synthesizing Risk-Cards
papers.abstract: The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in real-world applications has heightened the need for systematic, safety-oriented deployment frameworks. Existing approaches typically prioritize the construction of datasets and risk cards around the LLM and AI architecture itself, yet they provide scant consideration for the specific use-case that drives model selection. This omission is problematic because any practical AI deployment begins with a detailed use-case description that informs the assessment of contextual hazards. In this paper, we introduce a structured pipeline that, given a use-case, automatically produces a tailored dataset and an accompanying risk card. The process ensures that identified risks are tightly coupled to the use-case, and it offers traceable evidence from peer-reviewed literature to substantiate each risk to use-case relationship. Prior claim-verification methods (FActScore, FactReasoner) have been validated for factual claims. Risk-relevance is a hypothetical claim about possible harm, and whether evidence retrieval can meaningfully assess such claims remains untested. Literature-Informed Testbed for Mapping Use-cases and Synthesizing (LITMUS) risk cards are the first systematic attempt to characterize this adaptation. We evaluated the pipeline using the MIT Risk Taxonomy and achieved a 0.91 F1-score with a list of 320 samples from the benchmark risk dataset that was considered. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in generating robust, evidence-based risk assessments for LLM deployments.

papers.title: Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5Z: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
papers.abstract: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.

papers.title: An End-to-End Theory for Compositional Symbolic Execution: From Expressive Specifications to SMT (Extended Version)
papers.abstract: Compositional symbolic execution (CSE) is a powerful technique for program verification and bug-finding, yet existing formal theories of CSE do not sufficiently bridge the gap between idealised models and real-world tools. We present progress towards a foundational, realistic, end-to-end theory of CSE in the Rocq proof assistant. Our theory advances realism at both ends of the CSE pipeline: it supports an expressive frontend with algebraic data types, logical functions, and lemmas; it also provides a verified connection to SMT-LIB compliant SMT solvers. Our contributions include: (1) a CSE theory that captures practical verification patterns; (2) a standalone, reusable Rocq mechanisation of the SMT-LIB standard; (3) a proven-correct encoding from CSE backend queries to SMT-LIB queries that accounts for semantic discrepancies and optimises using type information; and (4) empirical evidence for the backend by extracting our verified SMT-LIB encoding and running it alongside the CSE tool Gillian's own encoding on a majority of its solver queries.

papers.title: Reporting Differential Privacy Guarantees via Operationally Equivalent $\varepsilon$: What Does $\varepsilon=19.61$ Mean for the 2020 U.S. Census?
papers.abstract: The large value $\varepsilon=19.61$, reported as an approximate differential privacy (ADP) parameter for the 2020 U.S. Census, has prompted doubts about the adequacy of Census privacy protection. This value was obtained by converting component guarantees expressed in zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP), an extension of differential privacy (DP), to ADP at $δ=10^{-10}$. Summarizing a guarantee by a single $(\varepsilon,δ)$ pair can substantially loosen its upper bound on the power (true positive rate) of a distinguishing test at a given significance level. We express the power bound from the original guarantee as the $α$-operationally equivalent $\varepsilon$, the smallest pure DP parameter yielding the same power bound at significance level $α$. The full operationally equivalent $\varepsilon$ curve represents the original bound exactly on $(0,1)$, even when that bound is nonconcave. We also characterize the curve's extrema over an interval of significance levels. When finite, they give the pure DP parameters whose power bounds enclose the original bound on that interval. The mapping preserves the ordering of guarantees by their power bounds at each significance level, whereas conversion to single ADP pairs or Gaussian DP (GDP) envelopes can reverse this ordering for Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms with equal noise variance. For the P.L. 94-171 redistricting data, we reproduce the reported $\varepsilon=19.61$ as the sum of rounded component ADP values. The published zCDP guarantee yields operationally equivalent $\varepsilon$ values of approximately $4.25$, $2.94$, and $3.18$ at significance levels of $1\%$, $5\%$, and $10\%$, respectively. These values convey the original guarantee's constraints on distinguishing attacks more clearly than does the reported value $\varepsilon=19.61$, which by itself places little restriction on the success of such attacks.

papers.title: Learning in the Passive Space: End-to-End Muti-Order Port-Hamiltonian Macromodeling
papers.abstract: Compact, passive state-space macromodels of interconnects and power-delivery networks are essential for stable transient signal- and power-integrity simulations. However, conventional flows require costly per-layout full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, while both traditional fitting and prior learning surrogates rely on post-hoc fitting or passivity perturbation that degrades accuracy without guaranteeing convergence. In this work, we propose an end-to-end macromodeling framework that learns directly in the passive space, mapping physical layout graphs to multi-order port-Hamiltonian (pH) macromodels. Specifically, our network encodes each layout graph into unconstrained matrix blocks and assembles them via a complete, prefix-nested pH parameterization that guarantees continuous-frequency passivity and stability by construction, yielding valid $k$-state macromodels via direct state slicing in one forward pass. To train all orders without reference realizations, we supervise the network directly on S-parameters through a progressive order-growth curriculum. Evaluated on 27k unseen test structures from a 270k-structure advanced-packaging dataset, our framework reduces mean S-parameter error by $42\%$ on average (up to $65\%$) over established macromodeling tools fitted to ground-truth EM responses, achieves zero passivity violations across $459{,}000$ exported models, and accelerates macromodel generation by $11{,}000$--$39{,}000\times$ ($36$--$85$~ms per layout).

papers.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
papers.abstract: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$. The codes $I^{n-1}J$, where $I$ and $J$ partition the alphabet, attain this bound when $n$ divides $q$, and Blackburn conjectured that for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the best such code is a maximum non-overlapping code. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes $I^{n-1}J$ with $|I|=(n-1)q/n$ and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.

papers.title: The Complexity of Oracle-Efficient Realizable Transductive Learning
papers.abstract: In realizable transductive online learning, the learner knows the entire sequence of $T$ instances in advance, and the labels are consistent with one of $N$ hypotheses. With explicit access to the hypothesis class, the halving algorithm makes at most $\log_2 N$ mistakes. Can a comparable guarantee be achieved using only polynomially many empirical risk minimization (ERM) queries? We answer this question negatively, even for a weighted-ERM oracle that optimizes arbitrary real-valued linear objectives and returns a complete maximizing hypothesis. For every fixed $β\in(0,1)$ and every randomized learner making polynomially many oracle queries, there exists a fixed realizable instance with exactly $N=2^{\lfloor T^β\rfloor}$ hypotheses on which the learner makes $Ω_β(\sqrt{T\log N})$ mistakes in expectation. This matches the agnostic-rate upper bound achieved by random playout using $O(T)$ oracle calls. The separation persists for much smaller classes as well: along a sequence with $\log N=Θ((\log T)^2)$, we establish a mistake lower bound of $\exp(Ω(\log T/\log\log T))$. Our main technical contribution is a composition lemma that combines two realizable prediction problems such that their mistake lower bounds add, up to a small loss, while keeping the growth of the combined hypothesis class under control. Iterating this lemma yields a family of hard instances spanning the desired parameter regimes, establishing a sharp separation between information-theoretic and oracle-efficient mistake guarantees.

papers.title: PSC-Gen: Physical Sequence Conditioning for Video Generation via Agentic Visual Planning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion models have enabled the synthesis of high-fidelity, visually compelling videos. However, despite being trained on internet-scale video data, understanding underlying physical laws and generating physically plausible dynamics remain challenging. To mitigate this, conditioning video generators on explicit physical reasoning has emerged as a promising direction. Nevertheless, existing conditioning approaches often fail to incorporate detailed physical guidance into generation, resulting in physically implausible motion or visual artifacts. We propose PSC-Gen, a training-free framework that employs an agentic approach to synthesize visual conditions and inject their core dynamics via low-frequency filtering. By iteratively planning physical states and verifying generated keyframes, our Physics Agent constructs visually and physically consistent keyframe sequences. We then interpolate these keyframes into a continuous physical sequence and inject only its low-frequency components, steering the video model to preserve physical dynamics while synthesizing fine visual details. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations across physics-informed and robotic manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that PSC-Gen faithfully follows instructions and generates physically plausible videos.

papers.title: Domain-Specific Self-Supervised Learning for Cuneiform Sign Representation
papers.abstract: Recognizing cuneiform signs is challenging: sign shapes vary across historical periods, scribal practices, and preservation conditions, while expert annotations are scarce. We study whether domain-specific self-supervised pretraining yields better cuneiform sign representations than generic natural-image pretraining. We pretrain a masked autoencoder, CuneiMAE, on over 900K unlabeled sign crops and compare it with ImageNet-pretrained MAE, CLIP, and DINOv2 on a 218-class sign recognition benchmark. CuneiMAE learns substantially stronger frozen representations (43.7% linear-probe accuracy vs. 25.2% for ImageNet-MAE), with gains over ImageNet-MAE on cross-period transfer. Under fine-tuning, CuneiMAE outperforms ImageNet-pretrained baselines on our internal benchmark, with the largest gains when labels are scarce (+20.4 pp over ImageNet-MAE with 1% of labels). On an external benchmark, CuneiMAE reaches 69.9% top-1 accuracy after fine-tuning, about 8 pp above the ResNet-18 baseline from prior work. Explicit structural priors, such as edge-guided masking and part bottlenecks, do not improve over standard masked reconstruction. Overall, domain-specific self-supervision shows strong performance on cuneiform recognition tasks, particularly when labels are limited.

papers.title: Improving the Improver: Semantic PID Control for Medical Agent Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: High-stakes vertical medical tasks, such as postoperative pathological staging and long-term survival prediction, demand multi-step clinical reasoning over heterogeneous evidence under weak supervision and high outcome uncertainty. While we first orchestrate CliAgent, a domain-tailored clinical agent workflow that systematically grounds predictions in multi-modal patient evidence, manually designed medical agents remain constrained by static, brittle rules. Moreover, existing recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods suffer from feedback ambiguity and severe development-set overfitting when evolving agents in high-noise medical domains. Focusing on improving the improver, we propose Semantic PID-RSI, an evidence-guided control-theoretic framework for medical agent self-improvement. Inspired by PID control, our improver evaluates candidate modification batches via three diagnostic roles: P isolates current clinical failure modes, I synthesizes longitudinal evidence from past trials, and D estimates response dynamics and regression risks (D-pre/D-post). Selected plans are compiled into behavior contracts for staged probing and independent adoption judging. Instantiated and validated on challenging oncology tasks (pT/pN staging and survival prognosis), evolving CliAgent with Semantic PID-RSI on a 3B-activated open-weight model achieves substantial gains (up to +6.27 C-index points), outperforming overfitting-prone RSI baselines and approaching the performance of frontier proprietary models (e.g., GPT-6 series) equipped with CliAgent.

papers.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
papers.abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, we study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

papers.title: Interpreting Diffusion Model Activations in Natural Language
papers.abstract: Interpreting the intermediate activations of diffusion models (DMs) is key to understanding how they generate images. Existing interpretability methods for DMs provide limited support for open-ended interrogation, making it difficult to extract human-interpretable insights. We extend LatentQA, the task of answering natural-language questions about Large Language Model activations, to DM activations. We introduce the Diffusion-specific Activation Oracle (DAO), which translates DM activations into natural-language answers to open-ended questions about the ongoing generation. Our experiments show that DAO can effectively describe the content of the final image from activations at early denoising steps. Additionally, we demonstrate that DAO captures the structure of the DM's activation space well enough to steer image generation toward target attributes. Furthermore, we show that attribution patching through DAO identifies DM components that contribute to visual attributes specified in natural language. Our code is available at https://github.com/yamanoko/dao/tree/main.

papers.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. The program retains images and computes directly on pixels, and its operations decide how this evidence is used in each task. During memory evolution, the same model traces failures in its visual trajectories to the operations that lost or misused evidence and revises them. It also rewrites the notes and analysis tools that guide later revisions, which then build on earlier findings and skip changes that have already failed. We evaluate EvoViM with three multimodal models on six tasks covering visual matching, spatial recall, and sequential decision-making, including three tasks with deferred queries. Across the six tasks, EvoViM improves the average score over AutoMem, the strongest baseline in the main comparison, by 31.3-47.6 points on held-out episodes. Programs written once from the initial environment instructions perform substantially worse, highlighting the value of interaction experience in shaping how visual evidence is retained and used. Code and dataset are available at https://evovim.github.io/.

papers.title: VG3R: Video Generation Model for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Video generation models are widely used as 3D priors for novel view synthesis and 3D scene generation. Fine-tuned for perception, generation models also excel at dense prediction such as depth estimation. However, methods that apply video generation models to 3D reconstruction either predict depth without cameras or generate geometry and estimate cameras through many iterative denoising steps, which makes them slower. In this paper, we present $\textbf{VG3R}$, which turns a pretrained video generation model into a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model. Our key observation is that such a model already captures the depth and camera motion of a video, but not in the form required for reconstruction. We introduce two components: $\textit{clip-level shift prediction}$, which corrects depth distortion caused by the unknown shift in decoded inverse depth, and a $\textit{multi-layer camera head}$, which predicts per-frame cameras parameters by combining features across transformer blocks. Using Wan2.1 as its video backbone, VG3R reconstructs a scene and estimate the camera of every frame without iterative denoising. It achieves the lowest ATE and reconstruction errors among methods built on video generation models, runs about 4 and 14 times faster than Aether and Geo4D. VG3R also demonstrates competitive depth estimation and 3D reconstruction performance compared with geometry foundation models. Project page: https://github.com/KTH-RPL/VG3R

papers.title: Photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light
papers.abstract: Recent reports of nonclassical intensity correlations in harmonic generation raised questions about whether strong harmonic correlations necessarily imply genuinely quantum behaviour. Here, we compare the low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical and bright squeezed vacuum sources. The latter generates strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and can be explained by the common fluctuations from the driving field. A visible scaling of the measured correlation function with mean harmonic flux is observed, which is well-explained by a click detector-response model.

papers.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms. Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.

papers.title: Grammar-as-a-Drafter: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding speeds up generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens that the target model verifies in one forward pass. Under structured outputs (JSON schemas, regular expressions, tool-call formats), the drafter works against a constraint it does not know, so its proposals for keys, delimiters, and indentation are often rejected or invalid, even though the grammar engine already knows the next tokens. We present Grammar-as-a-Drafter (GaaD), which makes the grammar a second drafter. Before each verify step, the scheduler merges the drafter's proposal with grammar-forced tokens (out-degree 1 in the grammar automaton) into one draft row of width $K$ (which can exceed the drafter's proposal length $K_M$): matching tokens are promoted to GRAMMAR, the proposal is truncated where it disagrees, and grammar tokens fill the remaining slots. The verify step accepts GRAMMAR drafts without computing their logits, composing with any drafter without adding kernels or compilation on the critical path. Because grammars fix text rather than tokens, accepting canonical GRAMMAR drafts with probability 1 preserves grammar validity but can shift the output distribution relative to grammar-masked decoding. We implement GaaD in vllm-torchtpu and an independent Rust serving runtime, and evaluate it on TPU v7x with MTP, DFlash, and n-gram drafters on a JSON character-profile benchmark. GaaD raises average acceptance length from 2.06 to 5.43 for MTP (Qwen3.5-0.8B; 1.99 to 5.31 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B), 1.57 to 4.13 for DFlash, and 1.30 to 3.64 for n-gram (Qwen3-4B), decoding 2.66-2.81x faster at batch size 1 and 1.14-1.70x faster at batch size 64. In the Rust runtime, MTP with GaaD is 2.23x faster on Qwen3.5-0.8B and 2.02x on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (1.22-1.69x at high concurrency). Under mixed traffic, GaaD finishes workloads 1.03-1.23x sooner while modestly raising plain-text TPOT.

papers.title: Preserving Orientation and Transition Order in Transition Network Analysis: A Directed Topological Proof of Concept
papers.abstract: Transition Network Analysis (TNA; tna, Nestimate) models learning as directed Markov transitions. While Nestimate also offers sequence-level higher-order models, clique-based topological tools lose directional structure: tna::cliques() returns unordered mutual subsets without homology or convergence-divergence asymmetry, and undirected persistent homology in Nestimate symmetrizes transitions into clique complexes, erasing edge orientation and triangle order. We evaluate four directed constructions on group_regulation (9 states): Dowker sink/source complexes, directed flag complexes ($dFl$), and regular GLMY path homology, compared against row-permutation and degree-preserving null models ($B = 20,000$). Across $τ\in [0.20, 0.28]$, $β_1^{dFl}$ exceeds the max-symmetrized clique complex $β_1^{\mathrm{sym}}$ by $1$; on $τ\in (0.239087, 0.290401]$ (e.g., $τ= 0.26$), $β_1^{\mathrm{sym}} = 0$ whereas $β_1^{dFl} = 1$, capturing the reciprocal consensus $\leftrightarrow$ plan loop (weights $0.3958, 0.2904$). On $τ\in (0.146825, 0.172081]$, $dFl$ also leaves the directed 3-cycle {consensus, coregulate, emotion} unfilled. Regular GLMY path homology gives $β_1^{\mathrm{path}} = 0$ across all thresholds (lower-tail $p = 0.012$ for its sum over $[0.14, 0.30]$ under row permutation, reflecting in-degree concentration). Dowker analysis reveals significant sink-source asymmetry: 20-21 sink vs. 0 source 2-simplices across $[0.20, 0.28]$ ($p = 0.002$ at $τ= 0.26$), driven by six behaviors converging onto consensus ($\mathrm{InStrength} = 2.667$). Thus, directed complexes unify feedback and sink convergence over one directed graph.

papers.title: A proof of the weighted Böttcher-Wenzel inequality conjectured by Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński
papers.abstract: For a positive definite matrix $ω$ with two smallest eigenvalues $λ_1\leλ_2$ and the weighted Frobenius norm $\|X\|_ω^2=\mathrm{Tr}(X^*Xω)$, Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński conjectured that $\|[A,B]\|_ω^2\le\frac{λ_1+λ_2}{λ_1λ_2}\|A\|_ω^2\|B\|_ω^2$ for all complex matrices $A,B$. We prove this inequality for real and for complex matrices of every size, by a short computer-free argument, and we determine the cases of equality. In fact $\|XZY-YZX\|_2\le\|Z\|_{(2),2}\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2$ for all complex matrices of compatible sizes, where $\|Z\|_{(2),2}$ is the Ky Fan $(2),2$ norm (the $\ell^2$ norm of the two largest singular values), and the constant is attained unless $X$ and $Y$ are $1\times1$ matrices; the conjecture is the case $Z=ω^{-1/2}$. The best constant is the square of a unitarily invariant norm of $Z$, which is convex, so it suffices to treat weights whose $n-1$ largest eigenvalues coincide. For these, an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors, written in bases adapted to the pair of unit vectors, reduces the conjecture to the positive semidefiniteness of an explicit $4\times4$ Hermitian matrix depending on a $2\times2$ matrix $B$ in a convex set defined by two weighted operator-norm bounds, and an explicit determinant identity writes its determinant as a sum of products of factors that are visibly nonnegative; the phases of the entries of $B$ enter only through $|\det B|^2$, so the real case is literally a special case. As a second theorem we prove, for every weight, a strengthening of the conjecture that is equivalent to the inequality for one matrix and all pairs of unit vectors; its best constant is again a convex function of $ω^{-1/2}$, and the same argument applies. We also read the inequality as a sharp bound for inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state.

papers.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
papers.abstract: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these "sealed worlds", we are able to test the accuracy and robustness of the workflows. We demonstrate the approach on four tasks built from CMS open data and present it as a way to reliably benchmark scientific work in experimental high-energy physics. At the time of writing, the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, reaches 60% of the score of the expert reference analyses on average, ahead of GPT 6 Astra at 38% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 31%. In individual sessions on one of the tasks, Gemini 4 Argon exceeds the reference. The benchmark is hosted at https://hep-ex-bench.github.io

papers.title: The standard filtration of Leavitt path algebras and topological full groups
papers.abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Martín Barquero, Martín González, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.

papers.title: TaskVICL: Task-Conditioned Decoder States for Visual In-Context Learning
papers.abstract: The usefulness of an in-context demonstration for a vision-language model (VLM) depends on both the query image and the task posed about it. Common retrievers rank examples by image similarity and ignore the task, while task-aware alternatives require answer generation, external encoders or retriever training. We ask whether the frozen target VLM's own decoder states, read before it answers, can select demonstrations directly. TaskVICL represents each image and task by a task-conditioned processing signature: the hidden states at the final input position across all decoder layers. Its training-free variant, TaskVICL-Raw, averages cosine similarities between corresponding layer states and passes the retrieved examples with their reference answers to the same VLM. Across two VLMs and eight classification and visual question answering datasets, Raw achieves the highest average accuracy among training-free retrievers, exceeding the strongest baseline by 3.30 points on Qwen3-VL and 1.41 on InternVL3.5, with gains carrying over to Gemma-3-12B. When the same NICO++ image is asked about its object or its context, Raw retrieves largely different demonstrations for the two questions and outperforms an image retriever given task-matched demonstrations. A lightweight shared projection, TaskVICL-Proj, adds further gains on classification. Controls show that task text at extraction drives most of the gains, and attention analysis describes how it shifts attention toward the classified object. These results support the target VLM's internal states as a practical basis for task-aware demonstration retrieval.

papers.title: Pulsar magnetospheres with stable dissipative current sheets
papers.abstract: Harris-type current sheets have been studied extensively with particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations that may exhibit unrealistic characteristics when they operate at effective Lundquist numbers far below astrophysical values. Furthermore, localized studies of the pulsar equatorial current sheet generally contain no systematic magnetic-field component normal to the current sheet. Such a component develops naturally in a global pulsar magnetosphere because reconnecting field lines connect the northern and southern magnetic hemispheres. For realistic Lundquist numbers, the normal magnetic field may suppress the tearing instability and control the dissipation in the pulsar equatorial current sheet. We derive the electromagnetic boundary conditions on the surface of the equatorial current sheet imposed by the surrounding ideal force-free magnetosphere and we incorporate them into a global force-free model that we solve with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). Preliminary solutions indicate two distinct magnetospheric configurations, a nearly ideal CKF-like state with negligible equatorial dissipation, and a strongly dissipative state resembling the solutions of Contopoulos et al. (2014) and Cerutti et al. (2015). These two classes of solutions may help us understand the phenomenon of mode switching in pulsars.

papers.title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
papers.abstract: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.

papers.title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). However, UI-API differences varied significantly across models for all sycophancy dimensions, including a pronounced reversal for DeepSeek moral sycophancy (43% UI vs. 82.3% API). Overall, our results suggest that API-based LLM evaluations may underestimate the prevalence of sycophancy in corresponding consumer-facing systems, making access conditions consequential for the external validity of LLM evaluation. To facilitate research on access-mode effects, we release 57,000 model responses and SycoUI, a browser-automation pipeline for standardized cross-interface LLM evaluation.

papers.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
papers.abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

papers.title: Pushdown Reachability Requires $N^2$ Time on Multitape Turing Machines
papers.abstract: Pushdown reachability, or equivalently, language non-emptiness of pushdown automata (PDA), is a fundamental problem in automata theory and program analysis. We show that, for every $ε>0$, no deterministic multitape Turing machine can decide pushdown reachability in $O(N^{2-ε})$ time, where $N$ is the input size. The lower bound already holds for \emph{sparse instances}, i.e., instances in which the number of transitions is linear in the number of states. This gives the first unconditional super-linear lower bound for pushdown reachability. Furthermore, we also extend this result and show that for any $ε> 0$ and $k \ge 1$, no deterministic multitape Turing machine can decide the intersection non-emptiness problem of one PDA and $k-1$ NFAs in time $O(N^{2k-ε})$, where $N$ is the input size. Finally, pushdown reachability is well-known to be quasi-linear time equivalent to many different problems in program analysis. Our result translates to all of those problems as well and provides the first unconditional super-linear lower bounds for those problems on multitape Turing machines.

papers.title: A pseudoscalar Higgs boson interfering with toponium: a QCD analysis of $\mathbf{gg\to A\to t\bar t}$ near threshold
papers.abstract: The CMS and ATLAS collaborations have observed an excess of $t\bar t$ events near threshold that is consistent with the formation of the pseudoscalar toponium state $η_t$. A pseudoscalar Higgs boson $A$ with a large coupling to top quarks could contribute part of this excess and the presence of the $A$ boson could be concealed. We point out that, if such a state exists with $M_A$ close to $2m_t$, it necessarily interferes with toponium, since both live in the colour--singlet ${}^1S_0$ channel and share the same Coulomb final--state interaction. Using exact leading--order amplitudes, whose relative phase is fixed by unitarity, and Coulomb resummation applied coherently to the QCD background, the $A$ boson signal and their interference, we show that the line shape is controlled by a single complex number $κ$, the ratio of the resonant and non--resonant amplitudes at the peak. Unitarity fixes ${\rm Im}\,κ=-1$ exactly when $A$ decays into top quarks, so that the interference reduces the resonant rate by $2/|κ|^2$ and produces an exact zero of the ${}^1S_0$ amplitude just above $M_A$. The parameter $κ$ does not depend on the $A$ coupling to top quarks and, with the Coulomb--enhanced width we find $|κ|\approx1.5$--$1.7$ for $M_A=350$--$380$ GeV and, hence, the $A$ resonance is completely distorted. For an $A$ boson accounting for 50\% (25\%) of the observed excess, it enhances the toponium peak by about 10 to 70\% (5 to 35\%), and the threshold excess differs strongly from the sum of the toponium and $A$ contributions.

papers.title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$μ$C
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $μ^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$μ$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$μ$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $μ^+$ and jet plane. We have also computed nuclear modification factors, that show a significant suppression, ranging locally between 30%-40%, depending on the observable.

papers.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result
papers.abstract: Formation control based on geometric constraints often requires either rigid interaction graphs or a common orientation reference. This paper investigates whether a prescribed planar formation can instead be achieved using only $N-1$ pairwise interactions while preserving global rotational freedom.
